title.zh: 卷四百八十九 列傳第二百四十八 外國五 占城 眞臘 蒲甘 邈黎 三佛齊 闍婆南毗 勃泥 注輦 丹眉流
title.en: Volume 489 Biographies 248: Foreign States 5 - Champa, Siem Reap, Bagan, Miaoli, Srivijaya, Sheponanpi, Brunei, Chola, Nakhon Si Thammarat
title.raw: 卷四百八十九 列傳第二百四十八 外國五 占城 眞臘 蒲甘 邈黎 三佛齊 闍婆南毗 勃泥 注輦 丹眉流 Volume 489 Biographies 248: Foreign States 5 - Champa, Siem Reap, Bagan, Miaoli, Srivijaya, Sheponanpi, Brunei, Chola, Nakhon Si Thammarat

sentences.zh: 占城 真臘 蒲甘 邈黎 三佛齊 闍婆南毗附 勃泥 注輦 丹眉流

translations.literal: Champa, Chenla, Bagan, Miaoli, Srivijaya, Sheponanpi (appended), Brunei, Chola, Tambralinga.
translations.idiomatic: Champa, Chenla, Bagan, Miaoli, Srivijaya, Sheponanpi (appended), Brunei, Chola, and Tambralinga.

sentences.zh: 占城國在中國之西南，東至海，西至雲南，南至真臘國，北至歡州界。

translations.literal: The state of Champa is southwest of China; east to the sea, west to Yunnan, south to the state of Chenla, north to the border of Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Champa lay to the southwest of China, bounded on the east by the sea, on the west by Yunnan, on the south by Chenla, and on the north by the frontier of Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泛海南去三佛齊五日程。

translations.literal: Sailing south across the sea, it is five days' journey to Srivijaya.
translations.idiomatic: By sea to the south, Srivijaya was five days' sail away.

sentences.zh: 陸行至賓陀羅國一月程，其國隸占城焉。

translations.literal: By land it is one month's journey to the state of Panduranga, which is subject to Champa.
translations.idiomatic: Overland, Panduranga was a month's march away; that country was under Champa's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 東去麻逸國二日程，蒲端國七日程。

translations.literal: East to the state of Mayi is two days' journey; to the state of Butuan, seven days' journey.
translations.idiomatic: To the east, Mayi lay two days away and Butuan seven.

sentences.zh: 北至廣州，便風半月程。

translations.literal: North to Guangzhou, with favorable winds, half a month's journey.
translations.idiomatic: Northward to Guangzhou was half a month under fair winds.

sentences.zh: 東北至兩浙一月程。

translations.literal: Northeast to the Two Zhe regions, one month's journey.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast to the Two Zhes was a month's journey.

sentences.zh: 西北至交州兩日程，陸行半月程。

translations.literal: Northwest to Jiaozhou, two days' journey; by land, half a month.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest to Jiaozhou was two days by sea or half a month overland.

sentences.zh: 其地東西七百里，南北三千里。

translations.literal: Its territory is seven hundred li east to west and three thousand li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory stretched seven hundred li from east to west and three thousand li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 南曰施備州，西曰上源州，北曰烏里州。

translations.literal: To the south is Shibei Prefecture, to the west Shangyuan Prefecture, to the north Wuli Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The southern region was called Shibei Prefecture, the western Shangyuan Prefecture, and the northern Wuli Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 所統大小州三十八，不盈三萬家。

translations.literal: It governs thirty-eight large and small prefectures, with fewer than thirty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: It ruled thirty-eight prefectures large and small, with fewer than thirty thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 其國無城郭，有百餘村，村落戶三五百，或至七百，亦有縣鎮之名。

translations.literal: The state has no walled cities; there are more than a hundred villages, with three to five hundred households per village, sometimes up to seven hundred, and there are also names of counties and market towns.
translations.idiomatic: The country had no walled cities, only more than a hundred villages of three to seven hundred households each, though some places bore the names of counties and market towns.

sentences.zh: 土地所出：箋沉香、檳榔、烏樠木、蘇木、白藤、黃蠟、吉貝花布、絲絞布、白�布、藤簟、貝多葉簟、金銀鐵錠等物。

translations.literal: What the land produces: fine aloeswood, areca, ebony, sappanwood, white rattan, yellow beeswax, kapok flower cloth, twisted-silk cloth, white cotton cloth, rattan mats, pattra-leaf mats, gold, silver, iron ingots, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Local products included fine aloeswood, areca nuts, ebony, sappanwood, white rattan, yellow beeswax, kapok cloth, twisted-silk fabrics, white cotton cloth, rattan and pattra-leaf mats, and ingots of gold, silver, and iron.

sentences.zh: 五穀無麥，有粳米、粟、豆、麻子。

translations.literal: Among the five grains there is no wheat; there are polished rice, millet, beans, and hemp seed.
translations.idiomatic: Wheat was not grown; the staple grains were polished rice, millet, beans, and hemp seed.

sentences.zh: 官給種一斛，計租百斛。

translations.literal: The government gives one hu of seed, and the assessed rent is one hundred hu.
translations.idiomatic: The state issued one hu of seed per allotment and collected rent at one hundred hu.

sentences.zh: 果實有蓮、甘蔗、蕉子、椰子。

translations.literal: Fruits include lotus, sugarcane, plantains, and coconuts.
translations.idiomatic: Fruits included lotus, sugarcane, plantains, and coconuts.

sentences.zh: 鳥獸多孔雀、犀牛。

translations.literal: Among birds and beasts there are many peacocks and rhinoceroses.
translations.idiomatic: Peacocks and rhinoceroses were especially common among the local fauna.

sentences.zh: 畜產多黃牛、水牛而無驢；

translations.literal: Livestock are mostly yellow cattle and water buffalo, and there are no donkeys;
translations.idiomatic: Livestock consisted mainly of cattle and water buffalo; there were no donkeys;

sentences.zh: 亦有山牛，不任耕耨，但殺以祭鬼，將殺，令巫祝之曰「阿羅和及拔」，譯云「早教他托生」。

translations.literal: There are also mountain cattle, unfit for plowing and hoeing; they are only killed to sacrifice to spirits. Before the killing, shamans are made to chant "A-luo-he ji ba," which translates as "May he be reborn early."
translations.idiomatic: Wild cattle too were found, but they could not be yoked for farming and were slaughtered only for spirit offerings; before each kill the shamans would intone "A-luo-he ji ba"—"May his soul pass quickly to rebirth."

sentences.zh: 民獲犀、象皆輸于王。

translations.literal: Whatever rhinoceros horn or elephants the people obtain, they all deliver to the king.
translations.idiomatic: Any rhinoceros horn or elephant taken by the people had to be surrendered to the king.

sentences.zh: 國人多乘象或軟布兜，或於交州市馬，頗食山羊、水兕之肉。

translations.literal: The people mostly ride elephants or soft-cloth litters, or buy horses at Jiaozhou markets; they often eat goat and water-buffalo meat.
translations.idiomatic: People commonly traveled by elephant or palanquin, or bought horses at Jiaozhou; goat and water-buffalo meat featured often in their diet.

sentences.zh: 其風俗衣服與大食國相類。

translations.literal: Their customs and dress resemble those of the Arab lands.
translations.idiomatic: Customs and dress resembled those of the Arab lands.

sentences.zh: 無絲蠶，以白ふ布纏其胸，垂至於足，衣衫窄袖。

translations.literal: There is no silk or sericulture; they wrap white cotton cloth about the chest, hanging to the feet, with narrow-sleeved upper garments.
translations.idiomatic: Silk was unknown; men wrapped white cotton from chest to ankle and wore narrow-sleeved jackets.

sentences.zh: 撮發爲髻，散垂余{髟肖}於其後。

translations.literal: They gather the hair into a topknot and let the remaining locks hang loose behind.
translations.idiomatic: Hair was gathered into a topknot with the rest left to hang down the back.

sentences.zh: 互市無緡錢，止用金銀較量錙銖，或吉貝錦定博易之直。

translations.literal: In mutual trade there is no strung cash; they use only gold and silver weighed to the zhu, or fix the value of barter with kapok brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Markets did without copper cash; trade was settled in gold and silver by weight, or valued in kapok brocade.

sentences.zh: 樂器有胡琴、笛、鼓、大鼓，樂部亦列舞人。

translations.literal: Musical instruments include the huqin, flute, drum, and large drum; the music office also arrays dancers.
translations.idiomatic: Instruments included the huqin, flute, drums, and great drum; the music office also fielded dancers.

sentences.zh: 其王腦後ヮ髻，散披吉貝衣，戴金花冠，七寶裝纓絡爲飾，脛股皆露，躡革履，無襪。

translations.literal: The king wears a topknot behind the head, a loose kapok robe, a golden flower crown, and ornaments of seven treasures set in necklaces; calves and thighs are bare; he treads leather sandals without socks.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a rear topknot and a loose kapok robe, a golden floral crown, and necklaces studded with the seven treasures; his calves and thighs were bare, and he went in leather sandals without stockings.

sentences.zh: 婦人亦腦後撮髻，無笄梳，其服及拜揖與男子同。

translations.literal: Women also gather the hair into a rear topknot, without hairpins or combs; their dress and bows are the same as men's.
translations.idiomatic: Women too wore rear topknots without pins or combs, and their dress and obeisances matched those of men.

sentences.zh: 王每日午坐禪椅。

translations.literal: The king sits on a meditation chair at noon each day.
translations.idiomatic: Each day at noon the king took his seat on a formal chair.

sentences.zh: 官屬謁見膜拜一而止，白事畢復膜拜一而退。

translations.literal: When officials come to audience they perform one prostration and stop; when they have reported their business they prostrate once more and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Officials paid one prostration on entering audience, reported their business, prostrated again, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 或出遊，看象、采獵、觀漁，皆數日方還。

translations.literal: Sometimes he goes out to view elephants, hunt, or watch fishing, and does not return for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Outings to watch elephants, hunt, or observe fishing could keep him away for days.

sentences.zh: 近則乘軟布兜，遠則乘象，或乘一木杠，四人舁之，先令一人持檳榔盤前導，從者十餘輩，各執弓箭刀槍手牌等，其民望之膜拜一而止。

translations.literal: For short distances he rides a soft-cloth litter; for long distances he rides an elephant, or rides a wooden pole carried by four men. First one man is sent ahead bearing an areca tray; more than ten followers each hold bow, arrow, knife, spear, hand shield, and the like; the people who see him perform one prostration and stop.
translations.idiomatic: Short journeys he made in a palanquin, long ones on elephant or a pole chair borne by four men, preceded by a servant with an areca tray and a dozen retainers armed with bow, blade, spear, and shield; commoners who sighted him prostrated once and held still.

sentences.zh: 日或一再出。

translations.literal: Some days he goes out once or twice.
translations.idiomatic: On some days he might appear in public once or twice.

sentences.zh: 每歲稻熟，王自刈一把，從者及群婦女競割之。

translations.literal: Each year when the rice ripens, the king himself reaps one handful, and his followers and crowds of women compete to reap the rest.
translations.idiomatic: At harvest each year the king cut the first handful himself, after which attendants and women of the court rushed to finish the reaping.

sentences.zh: 其王或以兄爲副王，或以弟爲次王。

translations.literal: The king sometimes appoints an elder brother as deputy king, or a younger brother as secondary king.
translations.idiomatic: The king might name an elder brother deputy ruler or a younger brother second king.

sentences.zh: 設高官凡八員，東西南北各二，分治其事，無奉祿，令其所管土俗資給之。

translations.literal: Eight high offices are established, two each for east, west, south, and north, to divide governance of affairs; they receive no salary but are supplied by the local customs of the districts they govern.
translations.idiomatic: Eight grand officers—two for each cardinal direction—shared administration without salary, living on levies from their districts.

sentences.zh: 別置文吏五十餘員，有郎中、員外、秀才之稱，分掌資儲寶貨等事，亦無資奉，但給龜魚充食及免調役而已。

translations.literal: Fifty-odd clerks are separately appointed, bearing titles such as langzhong, yuanwai, and xiucai, to divide charge of stores, treasure goods, and the like; they too have no salary but are given turtles and fish for food and exemption from corvée only.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty clerks—styled langzhong, yuanwai, and xiucai—oversaw stores and treasure without pay, receiving only fish and turtle for food and exemption from labor levies.

sentences.zh: 又有司帑廩者十二員，主軍卒者二百餘員，皆無月奉。

translations.literal: There are also twelve treasury granary officers and more than two hundred who command soldiers; none receive monthly salary.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve treasury officers and over two hundred military commanders likewise received no monthly stipend.

sentences.zh: 勝兵萬餘人，月給粳米二斛，冬夏衣布各三匹至五匹。

translations.literal: Effective troops number more than ten thousand; each month they are given two hu of polished rice, and three to five bolts of cloth for summer and winter clothing.
translations.idiomatic: The standing army exceeded ten thousand men, paid two hu of rice monthly and three to five bolts of cloth for summer and winter uniforms.

sentences.zh: 每夕，唯王升床而臥，諸臣皆寢於地蓐。

translations.literal: Each evening only the king mounts a bed to sleep; all the ministers sleep on ground mats.
translations.idiomatic: Each night only the king slept on a raised bed; his ministers slept on mats on the ground.

sentences.zh: 親近之臣見王即胡跪作禮，稍疏遠者但拱手而已。

translations.literal: Close ministers, on seeing the king, immediately kneel in foreign fashion and perform obeisance; those somewhat more distant merely clasp hands.
translations.idiomatic: Intimates knelt in foreign style on meeting the king; more distant officials merely clasped their hands.

sentences.zh: 其風俗，正月一日牽象周行所居之地，然後驅逐出郭，謂之逐邪。

translations.literal: Among their customs, on the first day of the first month they lead an elephant around the place where the king dwells, then drive it out beyond the suburbs—this is called "expelling evil."
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the new year they led an elephant around the royal residence and then drove it beyond the suburbs in a rite called "expelling evil."

sentences.zh: 四月有遊船之戲。

translations.literal: In the fourth month there is the pleasure-boat game.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth month brought boating festivities.

sentences.zh: 定十一月十五日爲冬至，人皆相賀，州縣以土產物帛獻其王。

translations.literal: They fix the fifteenth day of the eleventh month as the winter solstice; everyone congratulates one another, and prefectures and counties present local products and silks to their king.
translations.idiomatic: They reckoned the winter solstice on the fifteenth of the eleventh month, when people exchanged congratulations and districts sent local goods and cloth to the king.

sentences.zh: 每歲十二月十五日，城外縛木爲塔，王及人民以衣物香藥置塔上焚之以祭天。

translations.literal: Every year on the fifteenth day of the twelfth month, outside the city they bind wood into a tower; the king and the people place clothing and incense medicines on the tower and burn them to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of the twelfth month a wooden tower was erected outside the city; king and people piled garments and incense upon it and burned them as a sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 人有疾病，旋采生藥服食。

translations.literal: When people fall ill, they promptly gather fresh medicines and take them.
translations.idiomatic: The sick gathered fresh herbs and took them at once.

sentences.zh: 地不產茶，亦不知醞釀之法，止飲椰子酒，兼食檳榔。

translations.literal: The land does not produce tea, nor do they know the method of brewing; they drink only coconut wine and also eat areca.
translations.idiomatic: Tea was not grown and grain wine unknown; they drank coconut liquor and chewed areca.

sentences.zh: 刑禁亦設枷鎖，小過以四人拽伏於地，藤杖鞭之，二人左右更互捶撲，量其罪或五六十至一百。

translations.literal: Penal prohibitions also include cangues and fetters; for minor offenses four men drag the culprit prone to the ground and beat him with rattan rods, two men on left and right alternately striking, according to the crime from fifty or sixty to one hundred blows.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment included stocks and shackles; minor offenses brought a prone beating with rattan switches by four men, two alternating left and right, from fifty to a hundred strokes according to the fault.

sentences.zh: 當死者以繩系於樹，用梭槍舂喉而殊其首。

translations.literal: Those deserving death are bound with rope to a tree; a shuttle-spear is used to pound the throat and sever the head.
translations.idiomatic: Capital convicts were roped to a tree and their throats crushed with a spear-shaft until the head came off.

sentences.zh: 若故殺、劫殺，令象踏之，或以鼻卷撲於地。

translations.literal: For deliberate murder or robbery-murder, they make an elephant trample the culprit, or roll him to the ground with its trunk.
translations.idiomatic: Premeditated or robbery murder was punished by having an elephant trample the culprit or dash him to earth with its trunk.

sentences.zh: 象皆素習，將刑人，即令豢養之人以數諭之，悉能曉焉。

translations.literal: The elephants are all long trained; when about to execute a man, they have the keeper instruct them by counting, and they all understand.
translations.idiomatic: The elephants were thoroughly trained; before an execution the keeper counted out the command and the beasts understood perfectly.

sentences.zh: 犯奸者，男女共入牛以贖罪。

translations.literal: Adulterers, man and woman together, present an ox to redeem the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Adulterers, man and woman alike, redeemed their offense with an ox.

sentences.zh: 負國王物者，以繩拘於荒塘，物充而後出之。

translations.literal: Those who owe goods to the king are bound with rope in a desolate pond until the goods are made good, then released.
translations.idiomatic: Debtors to the crown were bound in a remote pool until the debt was satisfied, then freed.

sentences.zh: 其國前代罕與中國通。

translations.literal: In former ages this state rarely had contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times the kingdom had seldom dealt with China.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，其王釋利因德漫遣其臣莆訶散貢方物，有雲龍形通犀帶、菩薩石。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, its king Shili Yinde Man sent his minister Puhe San to present tribute goods, including a cloud-dragon patterned rhinoceros horn belt and bodhisattva stone.
translations.idiomatic: During Later Zhou's Xiande reign, King Shili Yinde Man sent the minister Puhe San with tribute including a cloud-and-dragon rhinoceros-horn belt and bodhisattva stone.

sentences.zh: 又有薔薇水灑衣經歲香不歇，猛火油得水愈熾，皆貯以璢璃瓶。

translations.literal: There were also rose water that sprinkled on clothing kept its fragrance for a year without fading, and fierce fire oil that blazed hotter when it met water—all stored in glass bottles.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent rose water whose scent on cloth lasted a year, and naphtha that burned fiercer when it touched water, all packed in glass vessels.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，其王釋利因陀盤遣使莆訶散來朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, its king Shili Yintuo Pan sent the envoy Puhe San to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: In 961 its king Shili Yintuo Pan sent Puhe San to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 表章書于貝多葉，以香木函盛之。

translations.literal: The memorial and letter were written on pattra leaves and placed in a fragrant-wood casket.
translations.idiomatic: Their petition was inscribed on pattra leaves and enclosed in a scented-wood box.

sentences.zh: 貢犀角、象牙、龍腦、香藥、孔雀四、大食瓶二十。

translations.literal: Tribute: rhinoceros horn, ivory, borneol, aromatic medicines, four peacocks, and twenty Arab bottles.
translations.idiomatic: The tribute included rhinoceros horn, ivory, borneol, aromatics, four peacocks, and twenty glass bottles from the western lands.

sentences.zh: 使回，錫齎有差，以器幣優賜其王。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, gifts were bestowed in graded amounts, and vessels and silks were generously granted to their king.
translations.idiomatic: On the envoy's return the court gave graded rewards and sent vessels and silks in generous favor to the king.

sentences.zh: 三年，又貢象牙二十二株、乳香千斤。

translations.literal: In the third year they again presented twenty-two tusks of ivory and a thousand jin of frankincense.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent twenty-two ivory tusks and a thousand jin of frankincense.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，其王悉利因陀盤遣使團因陀玢李帝婆羅貢馴象、牯犀、象牙、白氎、哥縵、越諾，王妻波良僕瑁、男占謀律秀瓊等各貢香藥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande, its king Xili Yintuo Pan sent envoys Tuan Yintuo Fen, Li Diboluo, and others to present tame elephants, male rhinoceros, ivory, white felt, ge brocade, yuenuo, while the king's wife Bolang Pumao, his son Zhan Moulu Xiujiong, and others each presented aromatic medicines.
translations.idiomatic: In 966 King Xili Yintuo Pan sent Tuan Yintuo Fen, Li Diboluo, and others with tame elephants, bull rhinoceros, ivory, white felt, patterned silks, and brocade; the queen Bolang Pumao, Prince Zhan Moulu Xiujiong, and others sent aromatics as well.

sentences.zh: 五年，又遣使李𠰢、李被瑳相繼來貢獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth year they again sent envoys Li [character] and Li Beicuo in succession to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 967 envoys Li [character] and Li Beicuo came in succession with further tribute.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，遣使貢方物雌象一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao, they sent envoys presenting local products including one female elephant.
translations.idiomatic: In 970 they sent tribute including a female elephant.

sentences.zh: 四年，悉利多盤、副國王李耨、王妻郭氏、子蒲路雞波羅等並遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Xiliduo Pan, the deputy king Li Nou, the king's wife the Guo clan, the son Pulujiboluo, and others all sent envoys to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 971 King Xiliduo Pan, Deputy King Li Nou, Queen Guo, Prince Pulujiboluo, and others all sent missions with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年，其王波美稅褐印茶遣使莆訶散來貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, its king Bomei Shuihe Yinchai sent the envoy Puhe San to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 972 King Bomei Shuihe Yinchai sent Puhe San again with tribute.

sentences.zh: 六年，又貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year they again presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 973 they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 七年，又貢孔雀傘二、西天烽鐵四十斤。

translations.literal: In the seventh year they again presented two peacock parasols and forty jin of western-region beacon iron.
translations.idiomatic: In 974 they sent two peacock parasols and forty jin of steel from the western regions.

sentences.zh: 九年，遣使朱陀利、陳陀野等來貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year they sent envoys Zhu Tuoli, Chen Tuoye, and others to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 976 envoys Zhu Tuoli, Chen Tuoye, and others arrived with tribute.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，其王波美稅陽布印茶遣使李牌來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, its king Bomei Shuiyangbu Yinchai sent the envoy Li Pai to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 977 King Bomei Shuiyangbu Yinchai sent Li Pai with tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年，其王及男達智遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year, the king and Nan Dazhi sent envoys to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 978 the king and Prince Nan Dazhi sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣使李木吒哆來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they sent the envoy Li Muzhaduo to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 979 the envoy Li Muzhaduo came with tribute.

sentences.zh: 六年，交州黎桓上言，欲以占城俘九十三人獻于京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Li Huan of Jiaozhou memorialized, wishing to present ninety-three Champa captives to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 981 Li Huan of Jiaozhou asked to send ninety-three Champa prisoners to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗令廣州止其俘，存撫之，給衣服資糧，遣還占城，詔諭其王。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong ordered Guangzhou to detain the captives, comfort and support them, give clothing and provisions, send them back to Champa, and issue an edict instructing their king.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered Guangzhou to hold the captives, clothe and feed them, and return them to Champa with an edict to their king.

sentences.zh: 七年，遣使乘象入貢，詔留象廣州畜養之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year they sent envoys who rode elephants to come with tribute; an edict ordered the elephants kept and raised at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 982 envoys arrived riding elephants; the court ordered the animals kept at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，獻馴象，能拜伏，詔畜于京畿寧陵縣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they presented a tame elephant that could bow and prostrate; an edict ordered it kept in Ningling County in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In 983 they sent a trained elephant that could bow and prostrate; the court housed it at Ningling in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，其王施利陀盤吳日歡遣婆羅門金歌麻獻方物，且訴爲交州所侵，詔答令保國睦鄰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, its king Shilituo Pan Wuri Huan sent the Brahmin Jingema to present local products and also complained of invasion by Jiaozhou; an edict replied ordering them to preserve the state and be friendly with neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: In 985 King Shilituo Pan Wuri Huan sent the Brahmin Jingema with tribute and a complaint of Jiaozhou aggression; the court replied urging him to guard his realm and live at peace with his neighbors.

sentences.zh: 三年，其王劉繼宗遣使李朝仙來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year, its king Liu Jizong sent the envoy Li Chaoxian to come with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 986 King Liu Jizong sent Li Chaoxian with tribute.

sentences.zh: 儋州上言，占城人蒲羅遏爲交州所逼，率其族百口來附。

translations.literal: Danzhou memorialized that the Champa man Puluo'e, pressed by Jiaozhou, led his clan of a hundred mouths to come and attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Danzhou reported that Puluo'e of Champa, harried by Jiaozhou, had brought a clan of a hundred souls to submit.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，廣州上言，雷、恩州關送占城夷人斯當李娘並其族一百五十人來歸，分隸南海、清遠縣。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year, Guangzhou memorialized that Lei and En prefectures had forwarded the Champa foreigner Sidang Li Niang and her clan of one hundred fifty people who had come to submit, assigned to Nanhai and Qingyuan counties.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Guangzhou reported that Lei and En had forwarded Sidang Li Niang of Champa with a clan of 150 who had come over; they were registered in Nanhai and Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年，廣州又言，占城夷人忽宣等族三百一人來附。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duangong, Guangzhou again reported that the Champa foreigner Huxuan and others, clans totaling three hundred one persons, had come to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In 988 Guangzhou reported that Huxuan of Champa and others—301 people in all—had submitted.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，新王楊陀排自稱新坐佛逝國。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua, the new king Yang Tuopai styled himself newly enthroned in the state of Funan.
translations.idiomatic: In 990 the new king Yang Tuopai proclaimed himself ruler of the renewed Funan realm.

sentences.zh: 楊陀排遣使李臻貢馴犀方物，表訴爲交州所攻，國中人民財寶皆爲所略。

translations.literal: Yang Tuopai sent the envoy Li Zhen to present a tame rhinoceros and local products; the memorial complained of attack by Jiaozhou, and that the people's property and treasure throughout the state had all been plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tuopai sent Li Zhen with a tame rhinoceros and other goods, protesting that Jiaozhou had attacked and plundered the people's wealth throughout the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 上賜黎桓詔，令各守境。

translations.literal: The emperor granted Li Huan an edict ordering each to guard his own borders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Li Huan an edict ordering both sides to keep to their borders.

sentences.zh: 三年，遣使李良莆貢方物。

translations.literal: In the third year they sent the envoy Li Liangpu to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In 992 Li Liangpu came with local tribute.

sentences.zh: 賜其王白馬二、兵器等。

translations.literal: They granted their king two white horses, weapons, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave the king two white horses, arms, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 本國僧淨戒獻龍腦、金鈴、銅香爐、如意等，各優賜之。

translations.literal: The native monk Jingjie presented borneol, golden bells, bronze censers, ruyi scepters, and the like; each was generously rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The Champa monk Jingjie offered borneol, gold bells, bronze censers, and ruyi; each gift was richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 至道元年正月，其王遣使來貢，奉表言：

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Zhidao, its king sent envoys to come with tribute, presenting a memorial that said:
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 995 the king sent envoys with tribute and a memorial reading:

sentences.zh: 前進奉使李良莆回，伏蒙聖慈賜臣細馬二匹、旗五面、銀裝劍五口、銀纏槍五條、弓弩各五張及箭等，戴恩感懼，稽首，稽首！

translations.literal: The former tribute envoy Li Liangpu has returned; I have received in your holy kindness two fine horses, five banners, five silver-mounted swords, five silver-wrapped spears, five each of bow and crossbow with arrows, and the like. Bearing this grace I am moved and fearful—kowtow, kowtow!
translations.idiomatic: When our envoy Li Liangpu returned, Your Majesty had graciously granted me two fine horses, five banners, five silver-hilted swords, five silver-shafted spears, five bows and five crossbows with arrows. Overwhelmed by such grace, I prostrate myself again and again.

sentences.zh: 臣生長外國，敻遠天都。

translations.literal: Your subject was born and raised in a foreign land, far from the celestial capital.
translations.idiomatic: I was born and raised in a distant land, far from the celestial capital.

sentences.zh: 竊承皇帝聖明，威德廣大，臣不憚介居海裔，遣使入朝。

translations.literal: I have heard that the emperor is sagely and enlightened, his authority and virtue vast; your subject did not shrink from dwelling on an island shore and sent envoys to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Your Majesty's sagacity and far-reaching power, I did not hesitate though I dwell on a distant shore, and sent envoys to your court.

sentences.zh: 皇帝不棄蠻夷山國，曲加優賜。

translations.literal: The emperor did not abandon this barbarian mountain state but bent to grant exceptional favors.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty did not disdain this barbarian mountain realm but showed exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 然臣自爲土長，聲勢尚卑，常時外國頗相侵撓，況以前民庶如芥，隨風星散，流離各不自保。

translations.literal: Yet your subject, as a local chief, still had low standing and force; neighboring states often encroached and harassed, and moreover formerly the people were like mustard seeds scattered by the wind, drifting apart, each unable to protect himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as a local chief my standing was still weak; neighboring states often harassed us, and my people had been scattered like chaff in the wind, each unable to fend for himself.

sentences.zh: 近蒙皇帝賜臣內閑駔駿及旗幟兵器等，鄰國聞之，知臣荷大國之寵，而各懼天威，不敢謀害。

translations.literal: Recently I received from the emperor fine horses from the inner stables, banners, weapons, and the like; neighboring states heard of it, knew your subject bore the great state's favor, and each feared the celestial majesty, not daring to plot harm.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty granted me fine steeds, banners, and arms, neighboring states learned that I enjoyed the great empire's favor; awed by your majesty, they no longer dared plot against me.

sentences.zh: 今臣一國安寧，流民來復，若非皇帝天德加護，何以至此！

translations.literal: Now your subject's whole state is at peace and the displaced people are returning—if not for the emperor's heaven-sent virtue and protection, how could it have come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Now my realm is at peace and exiles are returning—without Your Majesty's heaven-sent protection, how could this be!

sentences.zh: 臣之一國仰望仁聖，覆之如天，載之如地。

translations.literal: Your subject's whole state looks up to your benevolence and sagacity, covered as by heaven, borne as by earth.
translations.idiomatic: My whole kingdom looks up to your benevolence and wisdom—you cover us as heaven, you bear us as earth.

sentences.zh: 臣自思惟，鴻恩不淺。

translations.literal: Your subject reflects on himself: the great grace is not shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on myself, I know your grace is profound indeed.

sentences.zh: 且自天子之都至臣所居之國，涉海綿邈，不啻數萬里，而所賜之馬及器械等並安全而至，皆聖德之所及也。

translations.literal: Moreover, from the Son of Heaven's capital to the state where your subject dwells, crossing the sea is vast and remote, no less than tens of thousands of li, yet the granted horses and weapons all arrived safely—this is all within the reach of sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: From the imperial capital to my realm the sea journey spans tens of thousands of li, yet the horses and arms you sent all arrived safely—such is the reach of your sacred virtue.

sentences.zh: 自前本國進奉，未嘗有旌旗弓矢之賜，臣今何幸，獨受異恩！

translations.literal: From former times when this state presented tribute, there had never been gifts of banners, bows, and arrows; how fortunate is your subject today to receive this special grace alone!
translations.idiomatic: Never before had our tribute missions received banners, bows, and arrows—how fortunate am I to receive such singular favor!

sentences.zh: 此蓋天威廣被，壯臣土疆。

translations.literal: This is surely because celestial majesty spreads widely and strengthens your subject's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Surely this is because your heavenly majesty spreads far and strengthens my domain.

sentences.zh: 臣雖殞身無以上報。

translations.literal: Though your subject perish in body, he cannot repay this above.
translations.idiomatic: Even were I to give my life, I could not repay you adequately.

sentences.zh: 兼臣貢使往復，資給備至，恩重山嶽，不可具陳。

translations.literal: Moreover, your subject's tribute envoys come and go, provisions supplied to the utmost, favor heavy as mountains—cannot be fully stated.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your tribute envoys travel back and forth with every need fully supplied; your grace weighs like mountains and cannot be told in full.

sentences.zh: 今特遣專使李波珠、副使訶散、判官李磨勿等進奉犀角十株，象牙三十株，玳瑁十斤，龍腦二斤，沉香百斤，夾箋黃熟香九十斤，檀香百六十斤，山得雞二萬四千三百雙，胡椒二百斤，簟席五。

translations.literal: Now I specially send the dedicated envoy Li Bozhu, vice-envoy He San, investigating officer Li Moyou, and others to present ten rhinoceros horns, thirty elephant tusks, ten jin of tortoiseshell, two jin of borneol, one hundred jin of agarwood, ninety jin of layered yellow mature incense, one hundred sixty jin of sandalwood, twenty-four thousand three hundred pairs of shande chickens, two hundred jin of pepper, and five mat screens.
translations.idiomatic: I now specially dispatch the dedicated envoy Li Bozhu, the vice-envoy He San, the investigating officer Li Moyou, and others to present tribute of ten rhinoceros horns, thirty elephant tusks, ten jin of tortoiseshell, two jin of borneol, one hundred jin of agarwood, ninety jin of layered yellow mature incense, one hundred sixty jin of sandalwood, twenty-four thousand three hundred pairs of shande chickens, two hundred jin of pepper, and five mat screens.

sentences.zh: 前件物固非珍奇，惟表誠懇。

translations.literal: The foregoing items are indeed not rare treasures; they only express sincere earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: These gifts are not rare treasures in themselves; they serve only to express my sincere devotion.

sentences.zh: 臣生居異域，幸遇明時，不貴殊珍，惟重良馬。

translations.literal: Your subject was born in a foreign land and, by fortune, meets an enlightened age; he does not prize exotic rarities—only fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: I was born in a distant realm and am fortunate to live in an enlightened age; I do not value exotic curios, only good horses.

sentences.zh: 儻皇帝念及外國，不罪懇求，若使介南歸，願垂頒賜，臣之幸矣。

translations.literal: If the Emperor, mindful of foreign states, does not blame this earnest request, and when the envoy returns south, would bestow them—your subject's good fortune indeed.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty, remembering this foreign state, will not punish my earnest plea, and when my envoy returns south will grant horses as I ask, that would be my great fortune.

sentences.zh: 兼臣本國元有流民三百，散居南海，曾蒙聖旨許令放還，今有猶在廣州者。

translations.literal: Moreover, your subject's state originally had three hundred displaced people scattered in the Southern Sea; we once received a sacred edict permitting their release, and some still remain in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, my kingdom once had three hundred displaced subjects scattered along the southern coast; an imperial edict once permitted their return, and some still remain in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 本國舊有進奉夷人羅常占見駐廣州，乞詔本州盡數點集，具籍以付常占，令造舶船，乘便風部領歸國，冀得安其生聚，以實舊疆。

translations.literal: Our state formerly had the tribute tribesman Luo Changzhan stationed in Guangzhou; I beg an edict to this prefecture to muster them all, draw up a register and hand it to Changzhan, have him build ships, catch favorable winds, and lead them home in formation, hoping to settle their lives and people and strengthen the old frontier.
translations.idiomatic: A former Champa tribute agent, Luo Changzhan, is now in Guangzhou; I beg that the prefecture gather all our people there, register them, and entrust them to Changzhan to build ships and sail home on favorable winds, so they may restore their communities and repopulate our old territory.

sentences.zh: 至於萬里感恩，一心事上，臣之志也。

translations.literal: As for gratitude across ten thousand li and serving the throne with one heart—that is your subject's will.
translations.idiomatic: To feel gratitude across ten thousand li and serve the throne with undivided loyalty—that is my resolve.

sentences.zh: 上覽表，遣使詣廣州詢問，願還者悉付波珠。

translations.literal: The Emperor read the memorial and sent an envoy to Guangzhou to inquire; all who wished to return were handed over to Bozhu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial and sent an envoy to Guangzhou to inquire; all who wished to return were entrusted to Bozhu.

sentences.zh: 使還，復賜白馬二，遂爲常制。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, white horses were again bestowed—two—and this became the regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned, two white horses were granted again, and this became the standing custom.

sentences.zh: 占城國王楊普俱毗茶室離頓首言：臣聞二帝封疆，南止屆于湘、楚；

translations.literal: The King of Champa, Yang Pujupicha Shili, bows his head and says: Your subject has heard that the Two Emperors' domains southward stopped at Xiang and Chu;
translations.idiomatic: The King of Champa, Yang Pujupicha Shili, kowtows and says: I have heard that the domains of the Two Emperors in the south extended only to Xiang and Chu;

sentences.zh: 三王境界，北不及于幽燕。

translations.literal: the Three Kings' boundaries northward did not reach Youyan.
translations.idiomatic: and the realms of the Three Kings in the north did not reach Youyan.

sentences.zh: 仰矚昌時，實邁往跡。

translations.literal: Looking up at this flourishing age, it truly surpasses past traces.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing upon this flourishing age, it truly surpasses all that went before.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下乾坤授氣，日月儲英，出震居尊，承基御極。

translations.literal: Bow your head: the Emperor Your Majesty received qi from Heaven and Earth, stored brilliance of sun and moon, emerged from Zhen to take the honored seat, inherited the foundation to rule the pole.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before Your Majesty, who received the breath of Heaven and Earth and stored the radiance of sun and moon, who rose from Zhen to take the throne and inherited the foundation to rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 慈悲敷於天下，聲教被於域中。

translations.literal: Compassion spreads over the world; sound teaching covers the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your compassion spreads across the world, and your civilizing teaching covers the realm.

sentences.zh: 業茂前王，功芳徂後，蒼生是念，黃屋非心。

translations.literal: Achievements surpass former kings; merit fragrant to posterity; the common people are your care—the yellow canopy is not your heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your achievements surpass those of former kings, your merit will fragrance posterity; you care for the people, and the imperial canopy is not your heart's desire.

sentences.zh: 無方不是生靈，有土並爲臣妾。

translations.literal: No direction lacks living beings; every land is your subject and concubine.
translations.idiomatic: No place lacks living beings; every land is your subject.

sentences.zh: 真風遍佈，霈澤周行，凡沐照臨，共增聳抃。

translations.literal: True wind spreads everywhere; generous rain circles round; all who receive your radiance together increase in reverent joy.
translations.idiomatic: Your true influence spreads everywhere, your generous grace circles the realm; all who receive your radiance rejoice together.

sentences.zh: 臣生於邊鄙，幸襲華風。

translations.literal: Your subject was born on the frontier marches and, by fortune, inherits Chinese culture.
translations.idiomatic: I was born on the borderlands and am fortunate to partake of Chinese civilization.

sentences.zh: 蟻垤蜂房，聊爲遂性；

translations.literal: Ant mounds and bee hives suffice for following one's nature;
translations.idiomatic: Like ants in a mound or bees in a hive, we are content with our nature;

sentences.zh: 龍樓鳳閣，尚阻觀光。

translations.literal: dragon towers and phoenix pavilions still block the sight of splendor.
translations.idiomatic: yet the dragon towers and phoenix halls of your court still lie beyond our sight.

sentences.zh: 再念自假天威，獲全封部，鄰無侵奪，俗有舒蘇。

translations.literal: Again reflecting: by borrowing Heaven's majesty, we obtained intact fief and territory; neighbors did not seize; customs had ease and revival.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting again, by borrowing your heavenly majesty we have kept our territory intact, our neighbors do not encroach, and our people live in peace.

sentences.zh: 每歲拜遣下臣，問甯上國，蒙陛下恩沾行葦，福及豚魚，特因回人，頒賜戎器。

translations.literal: Each year we send subordinate ministers to inquire after the peace of the superior state; we received Your Majesty's grace reaching even trailing grass, blessing reaching even fish and swine; specially through returning envoys you bestowed military gear.
translations.idiomatic: Each year we send ministers to inquire after the peace of the empire; Your Majesty's grace reaches even the grass by the road and blesses even fish and swine; through returning envoys you specially granted us arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 臣本土惟望闕焚香，歡呼拜受，心知多幸，曷答洪恩。

translations.literal: Your subject's homeland only faces the palace gate to burn incense, shouting joy as we bow and receive; in heart we know great fortune—how repay vast favor?
translations.idiomatic: In my homeland we face your palace gate to burn incense and shout for joy as we bow and receive your gifts; we know ourselves deeply fortunate—how can we repay such vast kindness?

sentences.zh: 聖君既念于賓王，誠懇肯忘於述職。

translations.literal: The sage ruler already thinks of guest-kings; sincere earnestness will not forget to perform duty.
translations.idiomatic: Since the sage ruler already cares for vassal kings, we will not forget our duty of tribute.

sentences.zh: 今遣專信臣布祿爹地加、副使臣除逋麻瑕珈耶、判官臣皮霸抵一行人力等，部署土毛，遠充歲貢。

translations.literal: Now I send the dedicated envoy Bulu Dijia, vice-envoy Chuboma Xujiaye, investigating officer Piba Di, and a party of laborers and others to deploy local products and send them afar as annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: I now dispatch the dedicated envoy Bulu Dijia, the vice-envoy Chuboma Xujiaye, the investigating officer Piba Di, and their party to gather local products and send them as this year's tribute from afar.

sentences.zh: 雖表楚茅之禮，實懷魯酒之憂。

translations.literal: Though it displays the ritual of Chu's thatch, in truth it harbors the worry of Lu's wine.
translations.idiomatic: Though this presents the humble ritual of Chu's thatch, we truly fear it is like Lu's wine—too slight for the occasion.

sentences.zh: 虔望睿明，甫寬譴戮。

translations.literal: Reverently hoping for sagely clarity, briefly to widen pardon and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: We reverently hope for your sagely clarity and beg a brief easing of reproof.

sentences.zh: 專信臣等回日，軍容器仗耀武之物，伏願重加賜齎。

translations.literal: When the dedicated envoys return, military vessels, implements, and objects for displaying martial might—we humbly wish added bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: When our dedicated envoys return, we humbly beg additional gifts of military gear and implements for displaying martial might.

sentences.zh: 蓋念忝爲臣子，合告君親，服飾車輿，威儀斧鉞，不敢私制，惟望恩頒。

translations.literal: Considering that, as subjects, we ought to inform ruler and kin: dress, carriages, regalia, axes and halberds—we dare not make privately; we only hope for gracious distribution.
translations.idiomatic: As your subjects we ought to inform our sovereign: for dress, carriages, regalia, and weapons we dare not make our own—we only hope you will grant them from your grace.

sentences.zh: 幹冒冕旒，不任死罪。

translations.literal: Offending the imperial crown—we cannot bear the crime of death.
translations.idiomatic: In offending the imperial crown, we deserve death and cannot bear the guilt.

sentences.zh: 布祿爹地加言本國舊隸交州，後奔于佛遊，北去舊所七百里。

translations.literal: Bulu Dijia said: Our state formerly was subordinate to Jiaozhou, then fled to Foyou, seven hundred li north of the old place.
translations.idiomatic: Bulu Dijia reported that Champa had formerly been subject to Jiaozhou, then moved to Foyou, seven hundred li north of its former seat.

sentences.zh: 使還，賜物甚厚。

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned, the gifts bestowed were very generous.

sentences.zh: 大中祥府三年，國主施離霞離鼻麻底遣使朱氵孛禮來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the state ruler Shilixiali Bimadi sent the envoy Zhu Boli to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1010), King Shilixiali Bimadi sent the envoy Zhu Boli to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣使貢師子，詔畜于苑中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an envoy was sent presenting lions; an edict ordered them kept in the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1011), an envoy presented lions; an edict ordered them kept in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 使者留二蠻人以給豢養，上憐其懷土，厚給資糧遣還。

translations.literal: The envoy left two barbarians to tend and rear them; the Emperor pitied their longing for home, generously supplied provisions and grain, and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy left two natives to tend the lions; the Emperor pitied their homesickness, gave them generous provisions, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 八年，遣使波輪訶羅帝來貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the envoy Bolun Heluodi was sent to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1015), the envoy Bolun Heluodi was sent to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 訶羅帝因上言有弟陶珠頃自交州押馴象赴闕，今幸得見，欲攜以還。

translations.literal: Heluodi therefore submitted that his younger brother Taozhu had lately escorted tame elephants from Jiaozhou to the court; now, having been fortunate to see him, he wished to take him back.
translations.idiomatic: Heluodi reported that his younger brother Taozhu had recently escorted tame elephants from Jiaozhou to court and, now that they had met, wished to take him home.

sentences.zh: 許之，仍賜陶珠衣幣裝錢。

translations.literal: It was granted; Taozhu was also given robes, silks, and travel money.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted, and Taozhu was also given robes, silks, and travel funds.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年，其王屍嘿排摩惵遣使羅皮帝加以象牙七十二株、犀角八十六株、玳瑁千片、乳香五十斤、丁香花八十斤、豆蔻六十五斤、沉香百斤、箋香二百斤、別箋一劑六十八斤、茴香百斤、檳榔千五百斤來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxi, King Shihe Paimozhan sent the envoy Luopidijia to present seventy-two elephant tusks, eighty-six rhinoceros horns, a thousand pieces of tortoiseshell, fifty jin of frankincense, eighty jin of clove flowers, sixty-five jin of cardamom, one hundred jin of agarwood, two hundred jin of layered incense, one dose of special layered incense sixty-eight jin, one hundred jin of fennel, and fifteen hundred jin of betel nuts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxi (1018), King Shihe Paimozhan sent the envoy Luopidijia with seventy-two elephant tusks, eighty-six rhinoceros horns, a thousand pieces of tortoiseshell, fifty jin of frankincense, eighty jin of cloves, sixty-five jin of cardamom, one hundred jin of agarwood, two hundred jin of layered incense, sixty-eight jin of special layered incense, one hundred jin of fennel, and fifteen hundred jin of betel nuts.

sentences.zh: 羅皮帝加言國人詣廣州，或風漂船至石塘，即累歲不達矣。

translations.literal: Luopidijia said that when people of his state went to Guangzhou, if wind drove the ship to Shitang, several years might pass without reaching court.
translations.idiomatic: Luopidijia said that when his countrymen sailed to Guangzhou, if wind drove their ships to Shitang they might fail to reach court for years on end.

sentences.zh: 三年，使還，詔賜屍嘿排摩惵銀四千七百兩並戎器鞍馬。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the envoy returned, an edict bestowed on Shihe Paimozhan four thousand seven hundred taels of silver together with military gear, saddles, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1019), when the envoy returned, an edict granted Shihe Paimozhan four thousand seven hundred taels of silver along with arms, saddles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 海上又有蒲端國、三麻蘭國、勿巡國、蒲婆衆國，大中祥符四年祀汾陰，並遣使來貢。

translations.literal: On the sea there were also the states of Puduan, Sanmalan, Wuxun, and the Pupo peoples; in the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, when sacrifices were performed at Fenyin, they all sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the seas were also Puduan, Sanmalan, Wuxun, and the Pupo states; in the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1011), when the Fenyin sacrifices were performed, all sent envoys to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 先是，咸平、景德中，蒲端國主其陵數遣使來貢方物及獻紅鸚鵡。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Xianping and Jingde periods, the Puduan king Qiling had repeatedly sent envoys presenting local products and offering red parrots.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Xianping and Jingde reigns, the Puduan king Qiling had repeatedly sent envoys with local products and red parrots.

sentences.zh: 其後，國主悉離琶大遐至亦以金版鐫表來上，其使已絮漢上言：「伏見詔旨給賜占城使鞍勒馬、大神旗各二，乞如恩例。」

translations.literal: Afterward, the state ruler Xilipa Daxiazhi also came up with a memorial engraved on a gold plate; his envoy Yixu, speaking in Chinese, said: "We have seen an edict bestowing on the Champa envoy two saddled horses and two great spirit banners each; we beg the same gracious precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Later King Xilipa Daxiazhi also submitted a memorial engraved on a gold plate; his envoy Yixu petitioned in Chinese: "We have seen an edict granting the Champa envoy two saddled horses and two great spirit banners each; we beg the same gracious precedent."

sentences.zh: 有司以蒲端在占城下，請賜雜彩小旗五，從之。

translations.literal: The relevant office, holding that Puduan ranked below Champa, requested five variegated silk small banners—approved.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office, noting that Puduan ranked below Champa, proposed granting five variegated silk small banners; the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 天聖八年十月，占城王陽補孤施離皮蘭德加拔麻疊遣使李蒲薩麻瑕陀琶來貢木香、玳瑁、乳香、犀角、象牙。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year of Tiansheng, the Champa king Yangbu Gushili Pilandejiabamadie sent the envoy Li Pusamaxiatuopa to present agarwood, tortoiseshell, frankincense, rhinoceros horn, and ivory.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eighth year of Tiansheng (1030), King Yangbu Gushili Pilandejiabamadie sent the envoy Li Pusamaxiatuopa with agarwood, tortoiseshell, frankincense, rhinoceros horn, and ivory.

sentences.zh: 慶曆元年九月，廣東商人邵保見軍賊鄂鄰百餘人在占城，轉運司選使臣二人齎詔書器幣賜占城，購鄰致闕下，餘黨令就戮之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Qingli, the Guangdong merchant Shao Bao saw more than a hundred bandits of the Elin army in Champa; the transport commission selected two envoys bearing edicts, ritual objects, and silks to bestow on Champa, to purchase Lin and deliver him to court, and ordered the remaining followers executed on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Qingli (1041), the Guangdong merchant Shao Bao found more than a hundred soldiers of the rebel Elin in Champa; the transport commission sent two envoys with edicts, gifts, and silks to Champa to buy Lin and bring him to court, and ordered the rest executed.

sentences.zh: 明年十一月，其王刑卜施離值星霞弗遣使獻馴象三。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the following year, its king Xingbu Shilizhixingxiafei sent envoys presenting three tame elephants.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the following year (1042), King Xingbu Shilizhixingxiafei sent envoys presenting three tame elephants.

sentences.zh: 皇祐二年正月，又使俱舍唎波微收羅婆麻提楊卜貢象牙二百一、犀角七十九。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Huangyou, envoys again sent Jushelipo Weishouluobomatiyangbu presenting two hundred one ivory tusks and seventy-nine rhinoceros horns.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Huangyou (1050), envoys Jushelipo Weishouluobomatiyangbu again presented two hundred and one ivory tusks and seventy-nine rhinoceros horns.

sentences.zh: 表二通，一以本國書，一以中國書。

translations.literal: Two memorials—one in the state's script, one in Chinese script.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted two memorials, one in their own script and one in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，其使蒲思馬應來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, its envoy Pusima came to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year (1053), its envoy Pusima came to present local products.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐元年閏三月，其使蒲息陀琶貢方物，還至太平州，江岸崩，沉失行橐。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month of the first year of Jiayou, its envoy Puxituopa presented local products; returning to Taiping Prefecture, the riverbank collapsed and traveling bags sank and were lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month of the first year of Jiayou (1056), its envoy Puxituopa presented tribute; on the return journey at Taiping Prefecture the riverbank collapsed and his baggage was lost in the water.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，詔廣州賜銀千兩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, an edict granted Guangzhou one thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year (1057), an edict ordered Guangzhou to grant one thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 六年九月，又獻馴象。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the sixth year, tame elephants were again presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the sixth year (1061), tame elephants were again presented.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，廣西安撫經略司言：「占臘素不習兵，與交阯鄰，常苦侵軼；

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, the Guangxi pacification and frontier commissioner reported: "Chenla has never practiced warfare; it borders Jiaozhou and constantly suffers raids;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year (1062), the Guangxi pacification commissioner reported: "Chenla has never been skilled in war; it borders Jiaozhou and constantly suffers incursions;

sentences.zh: 而占城復近修武備，以抗交阯，將繇廣東路入貢京師，望撫以恩信。」

translations.literal: yet Champa has lately been repairing military preparations to resist Jiaozhou and will enter tribute to the capital by the Guangdong route—we hope they may be comforted with grace and trust."
translations.idiomatic: while Champa has recently been building up its defenses against Jiaozhou and will come to court by the Guangdong route; we ask that they be treated with grace and good faith."

sentences.zh: 五月，其使頓琶尼來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, its envoy Dunpani came to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, its envoy Dunpani came to present local products.

sentences.zh: 六月，賜其王施里律茶盤麻常楊溥白馬一，從其求也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, its king Shililü Chapanmachang Yang Pu was granted one white horse, acceding to his request.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, its king Shililü Chapanmachang Yang Pu was granted one white horse, as he had requested.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，其王楊卜屍利律陀般摩提婆遣使貢方物，乞市驛馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining, its king Yangbu Shililütuobanmotipo sent envoys presenting local products and begged to purchase relay horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xining (1068), King Yangbu Shililütuobanmotipo sent envoys with tribute and asked to buy relay horses.

sentences.zh: 詔賜白馬一，令于廣州買騾以歸。

translations.literal: An edict granted one white horse and ordered mules purchased at Guangzhou for the return journey.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted one white horse and ordered mules bought at Guangzhou for the return journey.

sentences.zh: 五年，貢璢璃珊瑚酒器、龍腦、乳香、丁香、蓽澄茄、紫礦。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, tribute of glazed coral wine vessels, borneol, frankincense, cloves, cubebs, and purple ore was presented.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1072), it presented glazed coral wine vessels, borneol, frankincense, cloves, cubebs, and purple ore.

sentences.zh: 七年，交州李乾德言其王領兵三千人並妻子來降，以正月至本道。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Li Qiande of Jiaozhou reported that its king had led three thousand troops with wives and children to surrender, arriving in his circuit in the first month.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1074), Li Qiande of Jiaozhou reported that the Champa king had led three thousand soldiers with their wives and children to surrender, arriving in the first month.

sentences.zh: 九年，復遣使來言：其國自海道抵真臘一月程，西北抵交州四十日，皆山路。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, envoys were again sent saying: from their state by sea route to Chenla was one month's journey; northwest to Jiaozhou forty days—all mountain roads.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1076), envoys again reported that from their country by sea to Chenla was one month's journey, and northwest to Jiaozhou forty days—all by mountain roads.

sentences.zh: 所治聚落一百五，大略如州縣。

translations.literal: Settlements under administration numbered one hundred fifty, broadly like prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The settlements they governed numbered one hundred fifty, roughly comparable to prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 王年三十六歲，著大食錦或川法錦大衫、七條金瓔珞，戴七寶裝成金冠，躡紅皮履。

translations.literal: The king was thirty-six years old, wearing great robes of Dashi brocade or Sichuan-pattern brocade, seven strands of gold necklaces, wearing a gold crown adorned with seven treasures, treading red leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The king was thirty-six, dressed in Arab or Sichuan brocade robes with seven gold necklaces, wearing a gold crown set with seven jewels and red leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 出則從者五百人，十婦人執金柈合貯檳榔，導以樂。

translations.literal: When he went out, five hundred followers; ten women held gold trays storing betel nuts, led with music.
translations.idiomatic: When he went abroad he had five hundred attendants; ten women carried gold trays of betel, and musicians went before him.

sentences.zh: 王師討交阯，以其素仇，詔使乘機協力除蕩。

translations.literal: When the imperial army attacked Jiaozhou, because they were old enemies, an edict ordered the envoy to seize the opportunity and cooperate in exterminating them.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army campaigned against Jiaozhou, an edict ordered Champa, as an old enemy of Jiaozhou, to seize the opportunity and help destroy them.

sentences.zh: 行營戰棹都監楊從先遣小校樊實諭旨。

translations.literal: Yang Congxian, superintendent of campaign war junks, sent the petty officer Fan Shi to convey the instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Congxian, superintendent of campaign war junks, sent the petty officer Fan Shi to convey the imperial instruction.

sentences.zh: 實還，言其國選兵七千扼賊要路，其王以木葉書回牒，詔使上之。

translations.literal: When Shi returned, he said their state selected seven thousand troops to block the rebels' vital routes; the king wrote a reply on tree leaves—the edict ordered the envoy to submit it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shi returned and reported that Champa had chosen seven thousand troops to block the enemy's key routes; the king wrote his reply on palm leaves, and an edict ordered the envoy to present it.

sentences.zh: 然亦不能成功。

translations.literal: Yet they also could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they still could not achieve success.

sentences.zh: 後兩國同入貢，占城使者乞避交人。

translations.literal: Later the two states both entered tribute; the Champa envoy begged to avoid the Jiaozhou people.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when both states presented tribute together, the Champa envoy asked to avoid the Jiaozhou envoys.

sentences.zh: 詔遇朔日朝文德殿，分東西立；

translations.literal: An edict ordered: on the first day of the month, audience at Wende Hall, standing east and west separately;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that on the first of the month they attend at Wende Hall and stand on east and west sides separately;

sentences.zh: 望日則交人入垂拱殿，而占城趨紫宸；

translations.literal: on the full moon the Jiaozhou people entered Chui'gong Hall while Champa hurried to Zichen;
translations.idiomatic: on the full moon the Jiaozhou envoys entered Chui'gong Hall while Champa went to Zichen Hall;

sentences.zh: 大宴則東西坐。

translations.literal: at great banquets they sat east and west.
translations.idiomatic: at great banquets they sat on the east and west sides.

sentences.zh: 元祐七年，又表言如天朝討交阯，願率兵掩襲。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanyou, they again memorialized that if the celestial court attacked Jiaozhou, they wished to lead troops in a surprise raid.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanyou (1092), they again petitioned that if the court attacked Jiaozhou, they wished to lead troops in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以交阯數入貢，不絕臣節，難以興師，答敕書報之，而以其使良保故倫軋丹、副使傍木知突爲保順郎將。

translations.literal: The court, because Jiaozhou had repeatedly entered tribute without ceasing subject status, found it hard to raise an army; a reply edict reported to them, and their envoy Liangbao Gulundan and vice-envoy Bangmu Zhituo were made Baoshun Lang generals.
translations.idiomatic: The court, because Jiaozhou had repeatedly presented tribute and never ceased its subject status, found it difficult to launch a campaign; it answered with an edict, and made the envoy Liangbao Gulundan and vice-envoy Bangmu Zhituo Baoshun Lang generals.

sentences.zh: 政和中，授其王楊卜麻疊金紫光祿大夫，領廉、白州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe period, its king Yangbu Madié was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Purple Pouch, and made prefect of Lian and Bai.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe era, King Yangbu Madié was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Purple Pouch and given the prefectures of Lian and Bai.

sentences.zh: 楊卜麻疊言身縻化外，不沾祿食，願得薄授奉給，壯觀小國，許之。

translations.literal: Yangbu Madié said his person was bound in the outer transformation, not touching salary provisions, and wished a modest grant of stipend to dignify the small state—granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yangbu Madié said that though he lived beyond the transform of civilization he received no salary, and asked for a modest stipend to dignify his small kingdom; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年，進檢校司空兼御史大夫、懷遠軍節度、琳州管內觀察處置使，封占城國王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanhe, he was promoted Acting Minister of Works concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Huaiyuan Army commissioner, Linzhou observation and disposition commissioner, and enfeoffed King of Champa.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanhe (1119), he was promoted to Acting Minister of Works and Censor-in-Chief, made commissioner of the Huaiyuan Army and Linzhou observation commissioner, and enfeoffed as King of Champa.

sentences.zh: 自是，每遇恩輒降制加封邑。

translations.literal: From this on, whenever grace was granted, an edict lowered to add enfeoffment lands.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever imperial grace was granted, an edict was issued to add to his fief.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，楊卜麻疊遣使入貢，遇郊恩，制授檢校太傅，加食邑。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, Yangbu Madié sent envoys to present tribute; meeting suburban grace, an edict appointed Acting Grand Tutor and added food fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyan (1129), Yangbu Madié sent envoys to present tribute; on a suburban grace occasion an edict appointed him Acting Grand Tutor and added to his food fief.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十五年，其子鄒時闌巴嗣立，遣使進方物，求封爵，錫宴於懷遠驛，以其父初封之爵授之，報賜甚厚。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Shaoxing, his son Zoushilianba succeeded and sent envoys presenting local products, seeking enfeoffment; a banquet was given at Huaiyuan Station, the title first granted his father was conferred on him, and return gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Shaoxing (1155), his son Zoushilianba succeeded, sent envoys with tribute seeking enfeoffment, was feasted at Huaiyuan Station, received his father's former title, and was richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 乾道三年，子鄒亞娜嗣，掠大食國方物遣人來貢，以求封爵，爲其國人所訴。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiandao, the son Zou Yana succeeded, plundered goods of the Dashi state and sent people to present tribute seeking enfeoffment, and was denounced by people of his state.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qiandao (1167), his son Zou Yana succeeded, seized goods from Arab merchants and sent envoys to seek enfeoffment, but was denounced by his own people.

sentences.zh: 詔卻之，遂不議其封。

translations.literal: An edict refused it; enfeoffment was then not discussed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict refused the request, and his enfeoffment was not considered further.

sentences.zh: 七年，閩人有浮海之吉陽軍者，風泊其舟抵占城。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, a Fujian man sailing to Jiyang Military Prefecture had wind moor his boat at Champa.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1171), a man from Fujian sailing to Jiyang Military Prefecture was driven by wind to Champa.

sentences.zh: 其國方與真臘戰，皆乘大象，勝負不能決。

translations.literal: That state was then at war with Chenla; both rode elephants; victory and defeat could not be decided.
translations.idiomatic: Champa was then at war with Chenla; both sides fought on elephants, and neither could prevail.

sentences.zh: 閩人教其王當習騎射以勝之，王大說，具舟送之吉陽，市得馬數十匹歸，戰大捷。

translations.literal: The Fujian man taught its king that he should practice mounted archery to win; the king was greatly pleased, fully equipped boats to send him to Jiyang, bought several tens of horses and returned, and the battle was a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian man taught the king to train in mounted archery to win; the king was delighted, sent him by ship to Jiyang, bought several dozen horses, and on returning won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 明年復來，瓊州拒之，憤怒大掠而歸。

translations.literal: The next year he came again; Qiongzhou refused him; in anger he plundered greatly and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned; Qiongzhou refused him entry, and in anger he raided widely before going home.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，嚴馬禁，不得售外蕃。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi, the horse ban was strictly enforced; they could not be sold to foreign states.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunxi (1175), the horse ban was strictly enforced and horses could not be sold to foreigners.

sentences.zh: 三年，占城歸所掠生口八十三人，求通商，詔不許。

translations.literal: In the third year, Champa returned eighty-three captives it had seized and sought trade; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1176), Champa returned eighty-three captives it had taken and asked to trade; an edict refused.

sentences.zh: 四年，占城以舟師襲真臘，傳其國都。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Champa with naval forces raided Chenla and reached its capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1177), Champa sent a fleet against Chenla and took its capital.

sentences.zh: 慶元以來，真臘大舉伐占城以復仇，殺戮殆盡，俘其主以歸，國遂亡，其地悉歸真臘。

translations.literal: From Qingyuan onward, Chenla launched a great campaign against Champa to take revenge, slaughtering nearly all, capturing its king and returning—the state then perished, and its lands all went to Chenla.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qingyuan era onward, Chenla launched a major campaign against Champa for revenge, slaughtered nearly everyone, captured the king, and Champa perished; its territory all passed to Chenla.

sentences.zh: 真臘國亦名占臘，其國在占城之南，東際海，西接蒲甘，南抵加羅希。

translations.literal: The state of Chenla is also called Zhanla; its country lies south of Champa, east bordering the sea, west joining Bagan, south reaching Garahi.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Chenla, also called Zhanla, lay south of Champa, bordered the sea on the east, adjoined Bagan on the west, and reached Garahi on the south.

sentences.zh: 其縣鎮風俗同占城，地方七千餘里。

translations.literal: Its counties and towns, customs and practices resemble Champa; the territory exceeds seven thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Its districts and customs resembled Champa's; its territory exceeded seven thousand li.

sentences.zh: 有銅台，列銅塔二十有四、銅象八以鎮其上，象各重四千斤。

translations.literal: There is a bronze terrace, arraying twenty-four bronze pagodas and eight bronze elephants to guard atop it; each elephant weighs four thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: It had a bronze terrace topped with twenty-four bronze pagodas and eight bronze elephants as guardians, each elephant weighing four thousand jin.

sentences.zh: 其國有戰象兒二十萬，馬多而小。

translations.literal: Its country has war elephants numbering nearly two hundred thousand; horses are many but small.
translations.idiomatic: It had nearly two hundred thousand war elephants; its horses were numerous but small.

sentences.zh: 政和六年十二月，遣進奏使奉化郎將鳩摩僧哥、副使安化郎將摩君明稽�等十四人來貢，賜以朝服。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Zhenghe, it sent the memorial-presenting envoy Fenghua Langjiang Jiumosengge, vice-envoy Anhua Langjiang Mojunming Jitiansi, and fourteen others to present tribute; court robes were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Zhenghe (1116), it sent the memorial envoy Fenghua Langjiang Jiumosengge, vice-envoy Anhua Langjiang Mojunming Jitiansi, and fourteen others to present tribute; they were granted court robes.

sentences.zh: 僧哥言：「萬里遠國，仰投聖化，尚拘卉服，未稱區區向慕之誠，願許服所賜。」

translations.literal: Sengge said: "A country ten thousand li distant, looking up to submit to holy transformation, still bound in barbarian dress—it does not match our slight admiration; we wish permission to wear what was bestowed."
translations.idiomatic: Sengge said: "We are a land ten thousand li away, come to submit to your holy rule, yet still wear our barbarian dress, which does not express our humble admiration; we beg leave to wear what you have granted."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，仍以其事付史館，書諸策。

translations.literal: An edict approved it, and the matter was also entrusted to the Historiography Institute to be written in the annals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request and ordered the Historiography Institute to record the affair in the dynastic annals.

sentences.zh: 明年三月辭去。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year they took leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They departed in the third month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，又遣郎將摩臘、摩禿防來，朝廷官封其王與占城等。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe, [Chenla] again sent the langjiang Mo La and Mo Tufang to come; the court officially enfeoffed its king on a par with Champa.
translations.idiomatic: In 1120 Chenla again sent the generals Mo La and Mo Tufang; the court enfeoffed its king with the same honors as the king of Champa.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，以郊恩授其王金裒賓深檢校司徒，加食邑，遂定爲常制。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, on the suburban grace, its king Jin Poubin Shen was appointed Acting Minister of Works, with added fief income; this was then fixed as the regular rule.
translations.idiomatic: In 1129, at the suburban sacrifice, King Jin Poubin Shen was made Acting Minister of Works with an enlarged fief, and this became the standing practice.

sentences.zh: 其屬邑有真里富，在西南隅，東南接波斯蘭，西南與登流眉爲鄰。

translations.literal: Among its subordinate settlements was Zhenlifu, in the southwestern corner; southeast it adjoined Bosilan, southwest it neighbored Tambralinga.
translations.idiomatic: One of its dependencies was Zhenlifu in the southwest; to the southeast lay Bosilan, and to the southwest Tambralinga.

sentences.zh: 所部有六十餘聚落。

translations.literal: Under its rule were more than sixty settlements.
translations.idiomatic: Its domain comprised more than sixty settlements.

sentences.zh: 慶元六年，其國主立二十年矣，遣使奉表貢方物及馴象二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qingyuan, its ruler had reigned twenty years; he sent envoys with a memorial presenting local products and two tame elephants.
translations.idiomatic: In 1200, after twenty years on the throne, its king sent envoys with a memorial, tribute goods, and two tame elephants.

sentences.zh: 詔優其報賜，以海道遠涉，後毋再入貢。

translations.literal: An edict generously increased the return gifts; because the sea route was a distant crossing, [they were told] hereafter not to present tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: The court enriched the return gifts but, citing the long sea voyage, forbade further tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 蒲甘國，崇寧五年，遣使入貢，詔禮秩視注輦。

translations.literal: The state of Bagan: in the fifth year of Chongning it sent envoys to present tribute; an edict ordered its ceremonial rank to be treated like Chola.
translations.idiomatic: Bagan first sent tribute in 1106; the court ranked its envoys equal to those of Chola.

sentences.zh: 尚書省言：「注輦役屬三佛齊，故熙寧中敕書以大背紙，緘以匣袱，今蒲甘乃大國王，不可下視附庸小國。

translations.literal: The Secretariat said: "Chola was subordinate to Srivijaya, so in the Xining period imperial letters used large-backed paper sealed in a casket wrapping; now Bagan is a great king and cannot be looked down upon like a subordinate small state.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat argued: "Chola was once subordinate to Srivijaya, so under the Xining reign edicts used large-backed paper in a casket wrap; Bagan is a great kingdom and must not be treated like a petty vassal.

sentences.zh: 欲如大食、交阯諸國禮，凡制詔並書以白背金花綾紙，貯以間金鍍管籥，用錦絹夾袱緘封以往。」

translations.literal: It is desired to follow the ritual for great states such as the Arabs and Jiaozhou: all imperial writs are to be written on white-backed brocaded gold-flowered silk paper, stored in gilt-bronze tubular cases, and sealed with brocade-silk double wrappings for dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: They asked that Bagan receive the same protocol as the Arabs and Jiaozhou: every edict on white-backed gold-flower brocade, kept in gilt bronze tubes, and sealed in double brocade wraps.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 邈黎國，元祐四年，般次冷移、四抹粟迷等齎于闐國黑汗王並本國王表章來。

translations.literal: The state of Miaoli: in the fourth year of Yuanyou, Pancilengyi, Simosumiti, and others brought memorials from the Black Khan of Khotan and from their own king.
translations.idiomatic: In 1089 envoys of Miaoli—Pancilengyi, Simosumiti, and others—arrived bearing memorials from the Black Khan of Khotan and from their own king.

sentences.zh: 有司以其國未嘗入貢，請視於闐條式。

translations.literal: The relevant offices, because that country had never presented tribute, requested that it be handled under the Khotan regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Because Miaoli had never before sent tribute, the ministries asked to treat it under the Khotan precedent.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 三佛齊

translations.literal: Srivijaya
translations.idiomatic: Srivijaya

sentences.zh: 建隆元年九月，其王悉利胡大霞里檀遣使李遮帝來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jianlong, its king Xilihu Daxialitan sent the envoy Li Zhedi to come to court and present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of 960 King Xilihu Daxialitan sent the envoy Li Zhedi to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，又遣使蒲蔑貢方物。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year, envoys were again sent; Pu Mie presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer another mission arrived; Pu Mie brought local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 是冬，其王室利烏耶遣使茶野伽、副使嘉末吒朝貢。

translations.literal: That winter, its king Shiliwuye sent the envoy Chaye Jia and vice-envoy Jiamo Zha to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That winter King Shiliwuye sent the envoy Chaye Jia and vice-envoy Jiamo Zha with tribute.

sentences.zh: 其國號生留，王李犀林男迷日來亦遣使同至貢方物。

translations.literal: Its country was called Shenliu; its king Li Xilin Nanmiri also sent envoys arriving together to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Shenliu sent its king Li Xilin Nanmiri's envoys on the same voyage with tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 三年春，室利烏耶又遣使李麗林、副使李鴉末、判官吒吒璧等來貢。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, Shiliwuye again sent the envoy Li Lilin, vice-envoy Li Yamo, and judge Tuotuobi and others to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 962 Shiliwuye again sent Li Lilin, vice-envoy Li Yamo, judge Tuotuobi, and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 回，賜以白嫠牛尾、白瓷器、銀器、錦線鞍轡二副。

translations.literal: On their return, they were granted white ox tails, white porcelain, silver vessels, and two sets of brocade saddles and bridles.
translations.idiomatic: On their return the court gave them white ox tails, white porcelain, silverware, and two brocade saddle sets.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，遣使李何末以水晶、火油來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, it sent the envoy Li Hemuo to present crystal and naphtha.
translations.idiomatic: In 971 the envoy Li Hemuo brought crystal and naphtha as tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年，又來貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, tribute was again presented.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute came again in 972.

sentences.zh: 七年，又貢象牙、乳香、薔薇水、萬歲棗、褊桃、白沙糖、水晶指環、琉璃瓶、珊瑚樹。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, tribute again: ivory, frankincense, rosewater, long-life jujubes, flat peaches, white sugar, crystal finger-rings, glass bottles, and coral trees.
translations.idiomatic: In 974 the mission brought ivory, frankincense, rosewater, long-life jujubes, flat peaches, white sugar, crystal rings, glass bottles, and coral.

sentences.zh: 八年，又遣使蒲陀漢等貢方物，賜以冠帶、器幣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, envoys including Pu Tuohan again presented local products; caps, belts, and ritual goods were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In 975 Pu Tuohan and others came with tribute and received caps, belts, and court gifts.

sentences.zh: 咸平六年，其王思離咮啰無尼佛麻調華遣使李加排、副使無陀李南悲來貢，且言本國建佛寺以祝聖壽，願賜名及鐘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianping, its king Silizhuoluowunifomadiao Hua sent the envoy Li Jiapai and vice-envoy Wutuo Linanbei to present tribute, stating that their country had built a Buddhist temple to pray for the emperor's longevity and begging a name and a bell.
translations.idiomatic: In 1003 King Silizhuoluowunifomadiao Hua sent Li Jiapai and vice-envoy Wutuo Linanbei with tribute, reporting that Srivijaya had built a temple to pray for the emperor's long life and asking for a name and a bell.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其意，詔以「承天萬壽」爲寺額，並鑄鐘以賜，授加排歸德將軍，無陀李南悲懷化將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor praised the intent; an edict took "Receiving Heaven, Ten Thousand Years of Life" as the temple name and also cast a bell to bestow; Jiapai was appointed General of Returned Virtue, and Wutuo Linanbei General of Cherishing Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended their devotion, named the temple "Receiving Heaven, Ten Thousand Years of Life," and sent a cast bell; Jiapai became General of Returned Virtue and Linanbei General of Cherishing Transformation.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，其王思離麻囉皮遣使李眉地、副使蒲婆藍、判官麻河勿來貢，許赴泰山陪位於朝覲壇，遣賜甚厚。
