translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, its king Silimaluopi sent the envoy Li Meidi, vice-envoy Pu Polan, and judge Ma Hewu to present tribute; they were permitted to take part at the Taishan fengshan on the Court Audience Mound, and the dispatch gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In 1008 King Silimaluopi sent Li Meidi, vice-envoy Pu Polan, and judge Ma Hewu with tribute; they were allowed to attend the Taishan fengshan at the Court Audience Mound and received lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，其王霞遲蘇勿吒蒲迷遣使蒲謀西等奉金字表，貢真珠、象牙、梵夾經、昆侖奴，詔許謁會靈觀，遊太清寺、金明池。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi, its king Xiadisuwutapuomi sent the envoy Pu Mouxi and others presenting a memorial written in gold characters, offering pearls, ivory, Sanskrit sutras, and Kunlun slaves; an edict permitted them to visit the Huiling Shrine and tour Taiqing Temple and Jinming Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In 1017 King Xiadisuwutapuomi sent Pu Mouxi and others with a gold-letter memorial, pearls, ivory, Sanskrit sutras, and Kunlun slaves; the court let them visit Huiling Shrine, Taiqing Temple, and Jinming Pool.

sentences.zh: 及還，賜其國詔書、禮物以慰獎之。

translations.literal: When they returned, an imperial letter and ritual objects were bestowed on their state to comfort and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: On their departure the court sent an edict and gifts to reward the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 天聖六年八月，其王室離疊華遣使蒲押陀羅歇及副使、判官亞加盧等來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year of Tiansheng, its king Shilidiehua sent the envoy Pu Yatuoluoxie and vice-envoys and judges including Yajialu and others to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1028 King Shilidiehua sent Pu Yatuoluoxie with vice-envoys and judges including Yajialu bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 舊制還國使人貢，賜以間金塗銀帶，時特以渾金帶賜之。

translations.literal: By old rule, envoys returning from tribute missions were granted belts with inlaid gold over silver; on this occasion they were specially given belts of pure gold.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys had usually received belts of inlaid gold on silver, but this time they were given belts of solid gold.

sentences.zh: 熙寧十年，使大首領地華伽囉來，以爲保順慕化大將軍，賜詔寵之，曰：「吾以聲教覆露方域，不限遠邇，苟知夫忠義而來者，莫不錫之華爵，耀以美名，以寵異其國。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xining, the great chief Dihuajialuo came and was made Grand General of Cherishing Submission and Cherishing Transformation; an edict favored him, saying: "I use civilizing influence to cover the realms, not limiting near or far; whoever knows loyalty and righteousness in coming, none is not granted a splendid rank, adorned with a fine name, to show special favor to their state.
translations.idiomatic: In 1077 the great chief Dihuajialuo arrived and was made Grand General of Cherishing Submission and Cherishing Transformation. The emperor's edict read: "My civilizing sway embraces all realms, near and far alike; any who come in loyalty and righteousness receive exalted rank and a glorious title, that their kingdom may be honored.

sentences.zh: 爾悅慕皇化，浮海貢琛，吾用汝嘉，並超等秩，以昭忠義之勸。」

translations.literal: You delight in the imperial transformation, float across the sea with tribute gems; I use you for praise, and advance you beyond ordinary grades, to display encouragement of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: You delight in our rule and cross the sea with tribute; I reward you with ranks above the ordinary, to encourage loyalty and righteousness."

sentences.zh: 元豐中，使至者再，率以白金、真珠、婆律薰陸香備方物。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng period, envoys came twice, generally bringing white gold, pearls, patchouli, eaglewood, and storax among local products.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng era (1078–1085) two missions came, usually bearing white gold, pearls, patchouli, eaglewood, storax, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 廣州受表入言，俟報，乃護至闕下。

translations.literal: Guangzhou received their memorial and reported upward; only after a reply were they escorted to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou took their memorial and reported to court; only after imperial approval were they escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 天子念其道里遙遠，每優賜遣歸。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, mindful that the route was remote, each time generously bestowed gifts and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of the long voyage, the emperor each time gave generous gifts and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 二年，賜錢六萬四千緡、銀一萬五百兩，官其使群陀畢羅爲寧遠將軍，官陀旁亞里爲保順郎將。

translations.literal: In the second year, sixty-four thousand strings of cash and ten thousand five hundred taels of silver were bestowed; the envoy Quntuobiluo was appointed General of Pacifying the Far, and Tuopang Yali was appointed Gentleman of Cherishing Submission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1079 the court gave sixty-four thousand strings of cash and 10,500 taels of silver; Quntuobiluo was made General of Pacifying the Far and Tuopang Yali Gentleman of Cherishing Submission.

sentences.zh: 畢羅乞買金帶、白金器物，及僧紫衣、師號、牒，皆如所請給之。

translations.literal: Biluo begged to buy a gold belt, white-gold vessels, and for monks purple robes, master titles, and certificates—all were granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: Biluo asked for a gold belt, white-gold vessels, and purple robes, monastic titles, and certificates for monks; all were granted.

sentences.zh: 五年，廣州南蕃綱首以其主管國事國王之女唐字書，寄龍腦及布與提舉市舶孫迥，迥不敢受，言於朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Guangzhou head of the southern foreign trade convoy, acting for his country in state affairs, had the king's daughter write in Tang script and send borneol and cloth to the maritime trade intendant Sun Jiong; Jiong dared not accept and reported to court.
translations.idiomatic: In 1082 the Guangzhou convoy chief, acting for the kingdom, had the king's daughter write in Chinese and send borneol and cloth to intendant Sun Jiong; Jiong refused the gifts and reported to court.

sentences.zh: 詔令估直輸之官，悉市帛以報。

translations.literal: An edict ordered their value estimated and paid into the treasury; all the cloth was purchased in return.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the goods appraised and paid to the treasury, then bought all the cloth in settlement.

sentences.zh: 五年，遣使皮襪、副使胡仙、判官地華加羅來，入見，以金蓮花貯真珠、龍腦撒殿。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, envoys Piwu, vice-envoy Huxian, and judge Dihuajialuo came, entered audience, and with a golden lotus vessel presented pearls and borneol scattered in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: That same year envoys Piwu, vice-envoy Huxian, and judge Dihuajialuo had audience and scattered pearls and borneol from a golden lotus vessel across the hall.

sentences.zh: 官皮襪爲懷遠將軍、胡仙加羅爲郎將。

translations.literal: Piwu was appointed General of Cherishing the Far; Huxian and Jialuo were appointed Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Piwu was made General of Cherishing the Far; Huxian and Jialuo were made gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 加羅還至雍丘病死，賻以絹五十匹。

translations.literal: Jialuo, on returning, died of illness at Yongqiu; fifty bolts of silk were sent as funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Jialuo died at Yongqiu on the homeward journey; the court sent fifty bolts of silk for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 六年，又以其使薩打華滿爲將軍，副使羅悉沙文、判官悉理沙文爲郎將。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, their envoy Sadahua Man was again made a general, and vice-envoys Luoxi Shawen and judge Xili Shawen were made gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The next year envoy Sadahua Man was made a general, and vice-envoys Luoxi Shawen and judge Xili Shawen were made gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，再入貢。

translations.literal: In the Shaosheng period, tribute was again presented.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era (1094–1098) the kingdom sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十六年，其王悉利麻霞囉陀遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Shaoxing, its king Xilimaxiatuotuo sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1156 King Xilimaxiatuotuo sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「遠人向化，嘉其誠耳，非利乎方物也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Far people turning to transformation—I praise their sincerity, not the profit of their local products."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Distant peoples who submit—I value their sincerity, not the worth of their goods.

sentences.zh: 其王復以珠獻宰臣秦檜，時檜已死，詔償其直而收之。

translations.literal: Their king again presented pearls to the chief minister Qin Hui; Hui was already dead, and an edict ordered their value compensated and the pearls taken in.
translations.idiomatic: The king again sent pearls to Chief Minister Qin Hui; Hui was already dead, so the court paid their value and took the pearls for the treasury.

sentences.zh: 淳熙五年，復遣使貢方物，詔免赴闕，館於泉州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunxi, envoys were again sent presenting local products; an edict excused them from coming to court and lodged them at Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1178 another tribute mission came; the court excused them from traveling to the capital and received them at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 闍婆國在南海中。

translations.literal: The state of Java is in the South Seas.
translations.idiomatic: Java lay in the South Seas.

sentences.zh: 其國東至海一月，泛海半月至昆侖國；

translations.literal: Its country eastward to the sea is one month; crossing the sea half a month reaches the Kunlun country;
translations.idiomatic: Eastward to the open sea was a month's sail; half a month by sea brought one to the Kunlun lands;

sentences.zh: 西至海四十五日，南至海三日，泛海五日至大食國。

translations.literal: westward to the sea forty-five days, southward to the sea three days; crossing the sea five days reaches the land of the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: westward forty-five days to the sea, southward three days to the sea, and five days' sailing south to the Arab lands.

sentences.zh: 北至海四日，西北泛海十五日至勃泥國，又十五日至三佛齊國，又七日至古邏國，又七日至柴曆亭，抵交阯，達廣州。

translations.literal: Northward to the sea four days; northwest, crossing the sea fifteen days reaches Brunei, again fifteen days to Srivijaya, again seven days to Koroh, again seven days to Chalieting, reaching Jiaozhou and arriving at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Northward four days to the sea; northwest, fifteen days by sea to Brunei, fifteen more to Srivijaya, seven to Koroh, seven to Chalieting, then overland to Jiaozhou and on to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其地平坦，宜種植，產稻、麻、粟、豆，無麥。

translations.literal: Its land is level and suited to planting; it produces rice, hemp, millet, and beans, but not wheat.
translations.idiomatic: The land was flat and fertile, yielding rice, hemp, millet, and beans but no wheat.

sentences.zh: 民輸十一之租，煮海爲鹽。

translations.literal: The people pay a tithe in rent; they boil sea [water] to make salt.
translations.idiomatic: The people paid a one-tenth land tax and boiled seawater for salt.

sentences.zh: 多魚、鱉、雞、鴨、山羊，兼椎牛以食。

translations.literal: There are many fish, turtles, chickens, ducks, and goats; they also slaughter cattle for food.
translations.idiomatic: Fish, turtles, poultry, ducks, and goats were plentiful; cattle were also slaughtered for meat.

sentences.zh: 果實有木瓜、椰子、蕉子、蔗、芋。

translations.literal: Fruits include papaya, coconut, plantain, sugarcane, and taro.
translations.idiomatic: Fruits included papaya, coconut, plantain, sugarcane, and taro.

sentences.zh: 出金銀、犀牙、箋沉檀香、茴香、胡椒、檳榔、硫黃、紅花、蘇木。

translations.literal: It produces gold, silver, rhinoceros horn and ivory, letter aloeswood and sandalwood, anise, pepper, betel, sulfur, safflower, and sappanwood.
translations.idiomatic: The country exported gold, silver, ivory, aloes and sandalwood, anise, pepper, betel, sulfur, safflower, and sappanwood.

sentences.zh: 亦務蠶織，有薄絹、絲絞、吉貝布。

translations.literal: They also devote themselves to sericulture and weaving; there are fine silk gauze, twisted silk damask, and cotton cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They also raised silkworms and wove fine gauze, twisted silk damask, and cotton cloth.

sentences.zh: 剪銀葉爲錢博易，官以粟一斛二斗博金一錢。

translations.literal: Silver leaf is cut for coin in trade; the government exchanges one qian of gold for one hu and two dou of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Silver leaf served as currency; the state traded one cash-weight of gold for one hu and two dou of grain.

sentences.zh: 室宇壯麗，飾以金碧。

translations.literal: Dwellings are magnificent, adorned with gold and green.
translations.idiomatic: Houses were grand, trimmed in gold and green.

sentences.zh: 中國賈人至者，待以賓館，飲食豐潔。

translations.literal: When Chinese merchants arrive, they are received in guesthouses with rich food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese merchants were lodged in guesthouses and served lavish meals.

sentences.zh: 地不產茶。

translations.literal: The land does not produce tea.
translations.idiomatic: Tea did not grow there.

sentences.zh: 其酒出於椰子及蝦蝚丹樹，蝦蝚丹樹華人未嘗見；

translations.literal: Its wine comes from coconuts and the shrimp-lure tree; the shrimp-lure tree Chinese have never seen;
translations.idiomatic: Wine was made from coconuts and from the shrimp-lure tree—a plant unknown in China;

sentences.zh: 或以桄榔、檳榔釀成，亦甚香美。

translations.literal: or it is fermented from areca or betel, and is also very fragrant and fine.
translations.idiomatic: areca and betel were also fermented into notably fragrant liquor.

sentences.zh: 不設刑禁，雜犯罪者隨輕重出黃金以贖，惟寇盜者殺之。

translations.literal: No penal statutes are established; miscellaneous offenders according to lightness or heaviness pay out gold to redeem—only robbers are killed.
translations.idiomatic: There were no written penal codes; lesser offenders paid gold according to the crime, but robbers were executed.

sentences.zh: 其王椎髻，戴金鈴，衣錦袍，躡革履，坐方床，官吏日謁，三拜而退，出入乘象或腰輿，壯士五七百人執兵器以從。

translations.literal: Its king wears a topknot, a gold bell, brocade robes, and leather sandals, sits on a square couch; officials attend daily, three bows and withdraw; going out he rides an elephant or a waist litter, with five to seven hundred stalwarts bearing weapons following.
translations.idiomatic: The king wore a topknot and a gold bell, brocade robes and leather shoes, and sat on a square couch. Officials called daily, bowed three times, and withdrew. He traveled by elephant or palanquin, escorted by five to seven hundred armed retainers.

sentences.zh: 國人見王皆坐，俟其過乃起。

translations.literal: When the people see the king they all sit; they rise only after he has passed.
translations.idiomatic: Subjects sat when the king approached and rose only after he had passed.

sentences.zh: 以王子三人爲副王。

translations.literal: Three princes of the royal house serve as deputy kings.
translations.idiomatic: Three princes served as deputy kings.

sentences.zh: 官有落佶連四人，共治國事，如中國宰相，無月奉，隨時量給土產諸物。

translations.literal: There are four officials called luojielian who jointly govern state affairs, like the Chinese chancellor; they have no monthly salary but are given local products and goods as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Four ministers called luojielian governed together like Chinese chancellors, without fixed salaries but receiving native goods as the court required.

sentences.zh: 次有文吏三百餘員，目爲秀才，掌文簿，總計財貨。

translations.literal: Next are more than three hundred clerical officers called xiucai, who keep documents and tally wealth and goods.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred clerks called xiucai kept records and accounts.

sentences.zh: 又有卑官殆千員，分主城池、帑廩及軍卒。

translations.literal: There are also nearly a thousand petty officials who respectively manage walled towns, treasuries, and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly a thousand lesser officials oversaw cities, treasuries, and troops.

sentences.zh: 其領兵者每半歲給金十兩，勝兵三萬，每半歲亦給金有差。

translations.literal: Those who command troops receive ten taels of gold every half year; crack troops number thirty thousand, and every half year gold is also given in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders received ten taels of gold every six months; the army numbered thirty thousand elite troops, likewise paid in gold on a graded scale.

sentences.zh: 土俗婚聘無媒約，但納黃金於女家以娶之。

translations.literal: Local custom in marriage betrothal has no go-between; one simply pays gold to the woman's family to take a wife.
translations.idiomatic: Marriages required no matchmaker—only a payment of gold to the bride's family.

sentences.zh: 五月遊船，十月遊山，有山馬可乘跨，或乘軟兜。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they tour by boat; in the tenth month they tour the mountains—there are mountain ponies one may ride, or one may ride a soft palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they held boat excursions; in the tenth, mountain outings on pony or sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 樂有橫笛、鼓板，亦能舞。

translations.literal: Music has transverse flutes and clappers, and they can also dance.
translations.idiomatic: Music featured flutes and clappers, and the people danced.

sentences.zh: 土人被發，其衣裝纏胸以下至於膝。

translations.literal: The natives let their hair hang loose; their dress wraps the chest down to the knees.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners wore their hair loose and wrapped cloth from chest to knee.

sentences.zh: 疾病不服藥，但禱神求佛。

translations.literal: In illness they do not take medicine, but only pray to spirits and seek the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: The sick took no medicine but prayed to spirits and sought the Buddha's aid.

sentences.zh: 其俗有名而無姓。

translations.literal: Their custom has names but no surnames.
translations.idiomatic: People bore personal names but no family surnames.

sentences.zh: 方言謂真珠爲「沒爹蝦羅」，謂牙爲「家囉」，謂香爲「昆燉盧林」，謂犀爲「低密」。

translations.literal: In their dialect they call pearls "modie xialuo," ivory "jialuo," incense "kundun lulin," and rhinoceros horn "dimi."
translations.idiomatic: In their tongue pearls were modie xialuo, ivory jialuo, incense kundun lulin, and rhinoceros horn dimi.

sentences.zh: 先是，宋元嘉十二年，遣使朝貢，後絕。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the twelfth year of Yuanjia of the Song [dynasty of Liu], envoys were sent to present tribute; afterward [contact] ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In 435 envoys had once presented tribute under the Liu Song, but contact then lapsed for centuries.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年十二月，其王穆羅茶遣使陀湛、副使蒲亞里、判官李陀那假澄等來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Chunhua, its king Muluo Cha sent the envoy Tuozhan, vice-envoy Pu Yali, judge Li Tuonajiacheng, and others to come to court and present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of 992 King Muluo Cha sent Tuozhan, vice-envoy Pu Yali, judge Li Tuonajiacheng, and others to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 陀湛云中國有真主，本國乃修朝貢之禮。

translations.literal: Tuozhan said that China has a true sovereign, and their country therefore restored the ritual of court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhan declared that China had a true Son of Heaven, and Java had therefore renewed the tribute rites.

sentences.zh: 國王貢象牙、真珠、繡花銷金及繡絲絞、雜色絲絞、吉貝織雜色絞布、檀香、玳瑁檳榔盤、犀裝劍、金銀裝劍、藤織花簟、白鸚鵡、七寶飾檀香亭子。

translations.literal: The king presented ivory, pearls, embroidered gold-flowered gauze and embroidered twisted silk damask, variegated twisted silk damask, variegated cotton twisted damask, sandalwood, tortoise-shell betel trays, rhinoceros-mounted swords, gold-and-silver-mounted swords, rattan woven flower mats, white parrots, and a seven-jeweled sandalwood pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent ivory, pearls, gold-embroidered gauze and damask, patterned silks and cottons, sandalwood, tortoiseshell betel trays, rhinoceros- and gold-mounted swords, rattan mats, white parrots, and a sandalwood pavilion inlaid with seven jewels.

sentences.zh: 其使別貢玳瑁、龍腦、丁香、藤織花簟。

translations.literal: The envoys separately presented tortoiseshell, borneol, cloves, and rattan woven flower mats.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys added tortoiseshell, borneol, cloves, and rattan mats of their own.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝貢使泛舶船六十日至明州定海縣，掌市舶監察御史張肅先驛奏其使飾服之狀與嘗來入貢波斯相類。

translations.literal: Earlier, tribute envoys on merchant ships took sixty days to reach Dinghai County in Ming Prefecture; the maritime trade supervising censor Zhang Su first reported by express the appearance of their dress and ornaments as resembling those of Persians who had come to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier missions had sailed sixty days to Dinghai in Ming Prefecture; censor Zhang Su reported that their dress resembled that of earlier Persian tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 譯者言云：今主舶大商毛旭者，建溪人，數往來本國，因假其鄉導來朝貢。

translations.literal: The interpreter said: the chief merchant Mao Xu, a man of Jianxi, has many times gone to their country and therefore borrowed his fellow townsman as guide to come to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Interpreters explained that the convoy chief Mao Xu of Jianxi, a frequent trader in Java, had guided the envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 又言其國王一號曰夏至馬囉夜，王妃曰落肩娑婆利，本國亦署置僚屬。

translations.literal: They also said the king's one title is Xiazhimaluoye, the queen is Luojian Sapoli, and their country likewise appoints subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: They gave the king's title as Xiazhimaluoye and the queen's as Luojian Sapoli, and said the realm maintained its own bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 又其方言目舶主爲「葧荷」，主妻曰「葧荷比尼贖」。

translations.literal: In their dialect they call the ship owner "bohuo," and the owner's wife "bohuo bi ni shu."
translations.idiomatic: In their language the ship owner was bohuo and his wife bohuo bi ni shu.

sentences.zh: 其船中婦人名眉珠，椎髻，無首飾，以蠻布纏身，顏色青黑，言語不能曉，拜亦如男子膜拜；

translations.literal: Among the women on the ship was one named Meizhu, with a topknot, no head ornaments, her body wrapped in barbarian cloth, complexion blue-black, speech unintelligible, bowing like the men in prostration;
translations.idiomatic: A woman aboard named Meizhu wore a topknot, no jewelry, and dark indigo wraps; her speech was unintelligible, but she bowed like the men.

sentences.zh: 一子，項戴金連鎖子，手有金鉤，以帛帶縈之，名阿嚕。

translations.literal: she had one child, on whose neck hung a gold chain, in whose hand was a gold hook tied with a silk cord, named Alu.
translations.idiomatic: She carried an infant named Alu with a gold chain at the neck and a gold hook tied to his hand with silk.

sentences.zh: 其國與三佛齊有仇怨，互相攻佔。

translations.literal: Their country and Srivijaya have enmity and repeatedly attack and seize from each other.
translations.idiomatic: Java and Srivijaya were at feud and raided one another repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 本國山多猴，不畏人，呼以霄霄之聲即出。

translations.literal: In their country the mountains have many monkeys unafraid of people; call with a xiaoxiao sound and they come out.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain monkeys there feared no one and emerged at a xiaoxiao call.

sentences.zh: 或投以果實，則其大猴二先至，土人謂之猴王、猴夫人，食畢，群猴食其餘。

translations.literal: If fruit is thrown, the two great monkeys come first—the natives call them the Monkey King and Monkey Lady—and after they have eaten, the troop of monkeys eats the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Throw fruit and two great monkeys—the Monkey King and Monkey Lady—ate first; the rest of the troop finished what was left.

sentences.zh: 使既至，上令有司優待；

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived, the emperor ordered the relevant offices to treat them generously;
translations.idiomatic: On their arrival the emperor ordered generous treatment;

sentences.zh: 久之使還，賜金幣甚厚，仍賜良馬戎具，以從其請。

translations.literal: after a long while the envoys returned, and gold and coins were bestowed very generously; good horses and armor were also granted according to their request.
translations.idiomatic: when they left, the gifts of gold and coin were lavish, and fine horses and armor were granted as they had asked.

sentences.zh: 其使云：鄰國名婆羅門，有善法察人情，人欲相危害者皆先知之。

translations.literal: The envoys said: a neighboring state is called Brahman; it has good dharma and can discern human feelings—those who intend mutual harm all know it beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys spoke of a neighbor called Brahman, whose holy law read men's hearts so that would-be harmers were known in advance.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年六月，遣使入貢，詔禮之如交阯。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Daguan, envoys were sent to present tribute; an edict ordered them received with ritual like Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1109 Java sent tribute again; the court received the envoys with the same ceremony as Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 又有摩逸國，太平興國七年，載寶貨至廣州海岸。

translations.literal: There was also the state of Ma-i; in the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo it loaded treasure goods and reached the Guangzhou coast.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Ma-i: in 982 it brought treasure cargoes to the Guangzhou coast.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，以南郊恩制授闍婆國主懷遠軍節度、琳州管內觀察處置等使、金紫光祿大夫、檢校司空、使持節琳州諸軍事、琳州刺使、兼御史大夫、上柱國、闍婆國王、食邑二千四百戶、實封一千戶；

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, by a southern suburbs grace edict the lord of Java was granted Huaiyuan Army commissioner, Linzhou circuit observing commissioner-in-chief, Golden Crowned Grandee Acting Minister of Works, holder of the staff of Linzhou military affairs, Linzhou prefect, also censor-in-chief, supreme pillar of state, king of Java, fief of two thousand four hundred households, actual enfeoffment one thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: In 1129, by a southern-suburb amnesty edict, the Java ruler received Huaiyuan Army commissioner, Linzhou circuit intendant, Golden Grandee and Acting Minister of Works, command of Linzhou forces, the prefecture itself, censor-in-chief, Supreme Pillar, King of Java, a nominal fief of 2,400 households and 1,000 enfeoffed households;

sentences.zh: 悉里地茶蘭固野可特授檢校司徒，加食邑實封。

translations.literal: Xilidi Chalanguye was specially granted Acting Minister of Works, with added fief and actual enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Xilidi Chalanguye was separately made Acting Minister of Works with an increased fief and enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，復加食邑五百戶，實封二百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, again added fief five hundred households, actual enfeoffment two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In 1132 his fief rose by five hundred households and his enfeoffment by two hundred.

sentences.zh: 南毗 附

translations.literal: Sheponanpi, appended section
translations.idiomatic: Sheponanpi (appended)

sentences.zh: 南毗國在大海之西南，由三佛齊風颿月餘可至。

translations.literal: The state of Sheponanpi is in the southwest of the great sea; from Srivijaya by wind sail a little over a month can reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Sheponanpi lay southwest across the ocean; from Srivijaya a fair wind carried one there in somewhat over a month.

sentences.zh: 其國王每巡行，先期遣兵百余人持水灑地上，以防颶風揚沙塵；

translations.literal: Whenever its king made a progress, beforehand he sent over a hundred soldiers holding water to sprinkle the ground, to guard against typhoon winds raising sand and dust;
translations.idiomatic: Before the king went abroad, he sent more than a hundred men to sprinkle the ground with water against typhoon-blown sand;

sentences.zh: 列鼎百以進食，日一易之，置翰林官供王飲食。

translations.literal: a hundred cauldrons were arrayed to present food, changed once a day; Hanlin officials were placed to supply the king's food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: he set out a hundred cauldrons for his meals, renewed daily, with palace stewards in charge of the king's board.

sentences.zh: 俗喜戰鬥，習刀槊，善射。

translations.literal: Their custom delights in battle; they practice blades and spears and are skilled at shooting.
translations.idiomatic: They loved war, trained with blades and spears, and shot well.

sentences.zh: 鑿雜白銀爲錢。

translations.literal: They chiseled mixed white silver to make coin.
translations.idiomatic: Coin was hammered from alloyed white silver.

sentences.zh: 產真珠、番布。

translations.literal: It produces pearls and foreign cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The land yielded pearls and imported cottons.

sentences.zh: 其國最遠，番舶罕到。

translations.literal: That state is most distant; foreign ships rarely arrive.
translations.idiomatic: It was among the farthest realms, and foreign vessels seldom called.

sentences.zh: 時羅巴智力幹父子，其種類也，居泉之城南。

translations.literal: At the time Luobazhili Gan, father and son—their kind—dwelt south of Quan's city.
translations.idiomatic: Luobazhili Gan and his son, men of that people, then lived south of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 自是，舶舟多至其國矣。

translations.literal: From then on, merchant ships mostly came to that country.
translations.idiomatic: After that, trading ships came to their shores in greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 勃泥國在西南大海中，去闍婆四十五日程，去三佛齊四十日程，去占城與摩逸各三十日程，皆計順風爲則。

translations.literal: The state of Brunei is in the southwest great sea; from Java forty-five days' journey, from Srivijaya forty days, from Champa and Ma-i each thirty days—all reckoned with fair wind as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Brunei lay in the southwestern ocean: forty-five sailing days from Java, forty from Srivijaya, thirty from Champa or Ma-i, all by fair wind.

sentences.zh: 其國以版爲城，城中居者萬餘人，所統十四州。

translations.literal: That country uses boards for its walls; in the city dwell over ten thousand people; it commands fourteen prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital was boarded like a stockade; more than ten thousand lived within, ruling fourteen districts.

sentences.zh: 其王所居屋覆以貝多葉，民舍覆以草。

translations.literal: Where the king dwells, the roof is covered with palmyra leaves; common houses are covered with grass.
translations.idiomatic: The king's halls were roofed in palmyra leaf, common roofs in thatch.

sentences.zh: 在王左右者爲大人。

translations.literal: Those at the king's side are called great men.
translations.idiomatic: Men at the king's side were styled the great men.

sentences.zh: 王坐繩床，若出，即大布單坐其上，衆舁之，名曰阮囊。

translations.literal: The king sits on a rope bed; if he goes out, he then sits on a great cloth sheet, the multitude lifts it—it is called Ruanang.
translations.idiomatic: The king sat on a corded couch; abroad he rode a great cloth litter borne by many, called a ruanang.

sentences.zh: 戰鬥者則持刀被甲，甲以銅鑄，狀若大筒，穿之於身，護其腹背。

translations.literal: Those who battle then take knives and don armor; the armor is cast of copper, shaped like a great tube, worn on the body to protect belly and back.
translations.idiomatic: Warriors carried blades in copper tube-armor cast to sheath belly and back.

sentences.zh: 其地無麥，有麻稻，又有羊及雞魚，無蠶絲，用吉貝花織成布。

translations.literal: That land has no wheat; it has hemp and rice; also goats and chickens and fish; no silk sericulture—they use kapok flowers woven into cloth.
translations.idiomatic: There was no wheat, but hemp, rice, goats, chickens, and fish; without sericulture, kapok was woven into cloth.

sentences.zh: 飲椰子酒。

translations.literal: They drink coconut wine.
translations.idiomatic: They drank coconut wine.

sentences.zh: 昏聘之資，先以椰子酒，檳榔次之，指環又次之，然後以吉貝布，或量出金銀成其禮。

translations.literal: Betrothal goods first use coconut wine, betel nuts next, rings again next, then use kapok cloth, or measure out gold and silver to complete the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Betrothal ran coconut wine first, then betel, then rings, then kapok cloth or measured gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 喪葬亦有棺斂，以竹爲輦，載棄山中。

translations.literal: Funeral burial also has coffin encoffment; a bamboo carrying-frame carries and abandons in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were coffined and borne on bamboo litters into the hills.

sentences.zh: 二月始耕則祀之，凡七年則不復祀矣。

translations.literal: In the second month when ploughing begins then they sacrifice to it; every seven years they no longer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: They sacrificed at the second month's sowing and ceased after seven years.

sentences.zh: 以十二月七日爲歲節。

translations.literal: They take the seventh day of the twelfth month as the year's festival.
translations.idiomatic: New Year fell on the seventh day of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 地熱，多風雨。

translations.literal: The ground is hot; wind and rain are many.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was hot and stormy.

sentences.zh: 國人宴會，鳴鼓、吹笛、擊鈸，歌舞爲樂。

translations.literal: When the country's people feast, they sound drums, blow flutes, strike cymbals, and sing and dance for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Feasts rang with drums, flutes, cymbals, song, and dance.

sentences.zh: 無器皿，以竹編貝多葉爲器盛食，食訖棄之。

translations.literal: They have no vessels—woven bamboo and palmyra leaves make vessels to hold food; when eating is finished they cast them away.
translations.idiomatic: They had no pottery: woven bamboo and palm leaf served as bowls and were discarded after the meal.

sentences.zh: 其國鄰于底門國，有藥樹，取其根煎爲膏，服之及塗其體，兵刃所傷皆不死。

translations.literal: That country borders Dimenguo; there is a medicinal tree, taking its root decocted into ointment—eating it and smearing the body, wounds from blades and weapons do not die.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring Dimen, they had a drug tree whose root salve, eaten or rubbed on the skin, was said to make blade wounds survivable.

sentences.zh: 前代未嘗朝貢，故史籍不載。

translations.literal: Former dynasties never had court tribute, so historical records do not record it.
translations.idiomatic: No earlier dynasty had received its tribute, and the histories had therefore been silent.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，其王向打遣使施弩、副使蒲亞里、判官哥心等齎表貢大片龍腦一家底、第二等八家底、第三等十一家底、米龍腦二十家底、蒼龍腦二十家底，凡一家底並二十兩；

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, its king Xiangda sent envoy Shenu, vice-envoy Pu Yali, judge Gexin and others bearing a memorial and presenting great-piece borneol one family bottom, second grade eight family bottoms, third grade eleven family bottoms, rice borneol twenty family bottoms, cang borneol twenty family bottoms—each family bottom together twenty taels;
translations.idiomatic: In 977 King Xiangda of Brunei sent Shenu, vice-envoy Pu Yali, judge Gexin, and others with tribute: top-grade borneol in one lot, eight second-grade lots, eleven third-grade, twenty lots each of rice- and pale borneol—each lot twenty taels;

sentences.zh: 龍腦版五、玳瑁殼一百、檀香三橛、象牙六株。

translations.literal: borneol boards five, tortoiseshell shells one hundred, sandalwood three wedges, ivory six stalks.
translations.idiomatic: plus five boards of borneol, a hundred tortoiseshells, three sandalwood logs, and six tusks of ivory.

sentences.zh: 表云：「爲皇帝千萬歲壽，望不責小國微薄之禮。」

translations.literal: The memorial said: "For the emperor's ten thousand years of life, I hope you will not blame this small state's meager gifts."
translations.idiomatic: Their memorial read: "For the emperor's ten thousand years, do not disdain our poor country's small offering."

sentences.zh: 其表以數重小囊緘封之，非中國紙，類木皮而薄，瑩滑，色微綠，長數尺，闊寸餘，橫卷之僅可盈握。

translations.literal: Its memorial used several layers of small pouches sealed closed—not Chinese paper, like tree bark yet thin, lustrous and smooth, color slightly green, several feet long, a foot wide, rolled crosswise barely filling the grip.
translations.idiomatic: The petition came in several little sealed pouches on a barklike leaf, not Chinese paper—thin, glossy, faintly green, a few feet long and a handspan wide, rolled crosswise to a fist's girth.

sentences.zh: 其字細小，橫讀之。

translations.literal: Its characters are minute, read crosswise.
translations.idiomatic: The writing was fine and read horizontally.

sentences.zh: 以華言譯之，云：「勃泥國王向打稽首拜，皇帝萬歲萬歲萬萬歲，願皇帝萬歲壽，今遣使進貢。

translations.literal: Rendered in Chinese speech it says: "The king of Brunei, Xiangda, bows his head and prostrates: emperor ten thousand years, ten thousand years, myriad myriad years; may the emperor ten thousand years of life; now sending envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Chinese it ran: "King Xiangda of Brunei kowtows: Long live the emperor ten thousand times ten thousand; may he live ten thousand years; I now send envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 向打聞有朝廷，無路得到。

translations.literal: Xiangda heard there was the court but had no road to reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangda had heard of the court but knew no road thither.

sentences.zh: 昨有商人蒲盧歇船泊水口，差人迎到州，言自中朝來，比詣闍婆國，遇猛風破其船，不得去。

translations.literal: Yesterday there was a merchant Pu Luxie whose ship moored at the estuary; I sent men to welcome him to the prefecture—he said he came from the Central Court, and on this trip was going to Java; he met fierce wind that broke his ship and could not go.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant named Pu Luxie had anchored at our river mouth; we fetched him to the prefect and learned he came from China but, bound for Java, had been wrecked by a storm and could not proceed.

sentences.zh: 此時聞自中國來，國人皆大喜，即造舶船，令蒲盧歇導達入朝貢，所遣使人只願平善見皇帝。

translations.literal: At this time hearing he came from China, the country's people were all greatly pleased, and immediately built a merchant ship, making Pu Luxie guide and reach to enter court tribute; the envoys sent only wish peacefully to see the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that he was from China, the people rejoiced and built a ship for Pu Luxie to guide our envoys to court; they asked only safe passage to behold the emperor.

sentences.zh: 每年令人入朝貢，每年修貢，慮風吹至占城界，望皇帝詔占城，令有向打船到，不要留。

translations.literal: Every year send people to enter court tribute, every year repair tribute—fearing wind blowing to Champa's border, hope the emperor will edict Champa that if Xiangda's ships arrive, do not detain them.
translations.idiomatic: They begged yearly tribute and annual embassies, and—lest storms drive them to Champa—that the emperor forbid Champa to detain Brunei vessels.

sentences.zh: 臣本國別無異物，乞皇帝勿怪。」

translations.literal: My native country otherwise has no other things; beg the emperor not to be angry."
translations.idiomatic: Our land has nothing else to offer; do not take offense.

sentences.zh: 其表文如是。

translations.literal: Its memorial text was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔館其使於禮賓院，優賜以遣之。

translations.literal: An edict lodged its envoys at the Court for Receiving Guests and generously bestowed gifts on sending them away.
translations.idiomatic: The court housed them at the Court for Receiving Guests and sent them home with generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年二月，其王錫理麻喏復遣使貢方物，其使乞從泉州乘海舶歸國，從之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Yuanfeng, its king Xilimano again sent envoys to present local products; the envoys begged to return home by sea vessel from Quanzhou, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1082 King Xilimano sent tribute again; his envoys asked to sail home from Quanzhou and were allowed.

sentences.zh: 注輦國東距海五里，西至天竺千五百里，南至羅蘭二千五百里，北至頓田三千里，自古不通中國，水行至廣州約四十一萬一千四百里。

translations.literal: The state of Chola is five li east from the sea; west to India one thousand five hundred li, south to Luolan two thousand five hundred li, north to Dundian three thousand li—from antiquity not connected to China; by water to Guangzhou approximately four hundred eleven thousand four hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Chola stood five li from the eastern sea: fifteen hundred li west to India, twenty-five hundred south to Luolan, three thousand north to Dundian—never linked to China before; by water Guangzhou lay some four hundred eleven thousand four hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 其國有城七重，高七尺，南北十二里，東西七里。

translations.literal: That country has walls in seven rings, seven feet high, twelve li north-south, seven li east-west.
translations.idiomatic: Seven concentric walls, each seven feet high, enclosed twelve li north to south and seven east to west.

sentences.zh: 每城相去百步，凡四城用磚，二城用土，最中城以木爲之，皆植花果雜木。

translations.literal: Each wall is one hundred paces apart; of the four walls brick is used, two walls earth, the innermost wall is of wood—all planted with flowers and assorted trees.
translations.idiomatic: The rings stood a hundred paces apart: four of brick, two of earth, the innermost of timber, all planted with flowers and fruit trees.

sentences.zh: 其第一至第三皆民居，環以小河；

translations.literal: The first to the third all are common people's dwellings, encircled by small rivers;
translations.idiomatic: The outer three rings held commoners, each ringed by a little moat;

sentences.zh: 第四城四侍郎居之；

translations.literal: the fourth wall four vice-ministers dwell;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth housed four vice-ministers;

sentences.zh: 第五城主之四子居之；

translations.literal: the fifth wall the ruler's four sons dwell;
translations.idiomatic: the fifth, the king's four sons;

sentences.zh: 第六城爲佛寺，百僧居之；

translations.literal: the sixth wall is Buddhist temples, a hundred monks dwell;
translations.idiomatic: the sixth was monastic, with a hundred monks;

sentences.zh: 第七城即主之所居，室四百余區。

translations.literal: the seventh wall is where the lord dwells, rooms exceeding four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: the seventh was the sovereign's compound of more than four hundred chambers.

sentences.zh: 所統有三十一部落，其西十二，曰只都尼、施亞盧尼、羅琶離鱉琶移、布林琶布尼、古檀布林蒲登、故里、娑輪岑、本蹄揭蹄、閻黎池離、舟阝部尼、遮古林、亞里者林；

translations.literal: It commands thirty-one tribal lands; twelve to the west: Zhiduni, Shiyaluni, Luopali Bepayiyi, Bulin Pabuni, Gutang Bulin Budeng, Guli, Suoluncen, Bentijieti, Yanlichi, Zhoubuni, Zhegulin, Yalizhelin;
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-one tribal lands obeyed it; twelve western—Zhiduni, Shiyaluni, Luopali Bepayiyi, Bulin Pabuni, Gutang Bulin Budeng, Guli, Suoluncen, Bentijieti, Yanlichi, Zhoubuni, Zhegulin, Yalizhelin;

sentences.zh: 其南八，曰無雅加黎麻藍、眉古黎苦低、舍里尼、密多羅摩、伽藍蒲登、蒙伽林伽藍、琶里琶離游、亞林池蒙伽藍；

translations.literal: eight to the south: Wuyajialimalan, Meiguliku, Shelini, Miduoluomo, Jialan Budeng, Mengjialinjialan, Palipali You, Yalinchi Mengjialan;
translations.idiomatic: eight southern—Wuyajialimalan, Meiguliku, Shelini, Miduoluomo, Jialan Budeng, Mengjialinjialan, Palipali You, Yalinchi Mengjialan;

sentences.zh: 其北十二，曰撥囉耶、無沒離江、注林、加里蒙伽藍、漆結麻藍、楃折蒙伽藍、皮林伽藍、浦棱和藍、堡琶來、田注離、盧婆囉、迷蒙伽藍。

translations.literal: twelve to the north: Boluoye, Wumolijiang, Zhulin, Jialimengjialan, Qijiemalan, Zanzhemengjialan, Pilinjialan, Pulengheland, Baopalais, Tianzhuli, Lubaluo, Mimengjialan.
translations.idiomatic: twelve northern—Boluoye, Wumolijiang, Zhulin, Jialimengjialan, Qijiemalan, Zanzhemengjialan, Pilinjialan, Pulengheland, Baopalais, Tianzhuli, Lubaluo, Mimengjialan.

sentences.zh: 今國主相傳三世矣。

translations.literal: The present state's lord has been transmitted through three generations.
translations.idiomatic: The ruling line had passed three generations.

sentences.zh: 民有罪，即命侍郎一員處治之，輕者縶於木格，笞五十至一百；

translations.literal: When commoners commit crime, then ordered one vice-minister to dispose of it; light offenders are bound on a wooden frame, flogged fifty to a hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Common criminals were judged by a vice-minister: light cases meant stocks and fifty to a hundred blows;

sentences.zh: 重者即斬，或以象踐殺之。

translations.literal: severe ones are beheaded, or trampled to death by elephants.
translations.idiomatic: grave ones brought beheading or crushing by elephant.

sentences.zh: 其宴，則國主與四侍郎膜拜于階，遂共坐作樂歌舞，不飲酒，而食肉。

translations.literal: At their feasts, the state's lord and four vice-ministers bow and prostrate on the steps, then together sit making music singing and dancing; they do not drink wine but eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: At court feasts the king and four vice-ministers kowtowed on the stairs, then sat to music and dance, eating meat but no wine.

sentences.zh: 俗衣布。

translations.literal: Their custom is to wear cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Dress was plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 亦有餅餌。

translations.literal: They also have cakes and pastries.
translations.idiomatic: They made cakes and dumplings as well.

sentences.zh: 掌饌執事用婦人。

translations.literal: Those in charge of food service use women.
translations.idiomatic: Women managed the royal kitchen.

sentences.zh: 其嫁娶，先用金銀指環使媒婦至女家，後二日，會男家親族，約以土田、生畜、檳榔酒等，稱其有無爲禮；

translations.literal: Their marrying: first use gold and silver rings making the matchmaker go to the woman's house; after two days, gather the man's kin, stipulate fields, livestock, betel wine and the like, calling whether they have them as the gift;
translations.idiomatic: Marriage began with gold and silver rings sent by a matchmaker; two days later the groom's kin pledged fields, cattle, betel wine, and whatever they could muster;

sentences.zh: 女家復以金銀指環、越諾布及女所服錦衣遣婿。

translations.literal: the woman's house in turn with gold and silver rings, Yuenuo cloth and brocade garments the woman wore sent to the groom.
translations.idiomatic: the bride's kin returned rings, Yuenuo cloth, and the silks she had worn.

sentences.zh: 若男欲離女則不取聘財，女卻男則倍償之。

translations.literal: If the man wishes to leave the woman then betrothal goods are not taken; if the woman rejects the man then compensation is doubled.
translations.idiomatic: If the husband repudiated her he forfeited the bride-price; if she left him she paid double.

sentences.zh: 其兵陣，用象居前，小牌次之，梭槍次之，長刀又次之，弓矢在後，四侍郎分領其衆。

translations.literal: Their battle array: elephants placed in front, small shields next, shuttle-spears next, long knives again next, bows and arrows at the rear; four vice-ministers each lead their hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Their order of battle ran elephants, then bucklers, javelins, long blades, and archers in the rear, the four vice-ministers each commanding a division.

sentences.zh: 國東南約二千五百里有悉蘭池國，或相侵伐。

translations.literal: Southeast of the country about two thousand five hundred li is the state of Xilan Pond; they sometimes mutually invade and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Some twenty-five hundred li southeast lay Xilan Pond, with which they fought off and on.

sentences.zh: 地產真珠、象牙、珊瑚、頗黎、檳榔、豆蔻、吉貝布。

translations.literal: The land produces pearls, ivory, coral, glass, betel, cardamom, kapok cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Pearls, ivory, coral, glass, betel, cardamom, and kapok came from the realm.

sentences.zh: 獸有山羊、黃牛。

translations.literal: Beasts have mountain goats, yellow cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts included mountain goats and yellow cattle.

sentences.zh: 禽有山雞、鸚鵡。

translations.literal: Birds have mountain fowl, parrots.
translations.idiomatic: Among birds were jungle fowl and parrots.

sentences.zh: 果有餘甘、藤羅、千年棗、椰子、甘羅、昆侖梅、婆羅密等。

translations.literal: Fruits have yugan, tengluo, thousand-year jujubes, coconuts, ganluo, Kunlun plum, jackfruit and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Fruits ranged from yugan and rattan fruit to millennium jujubes, coconuts, ganluo, Kunlun plums, jackfruit, and more.

sentences.zh: 花有白末利、散絲、蛇臍、佛桑、麗秋、青黃碧娑羅、瑤蓮、蟬紫、水蕉之類。

translations.literal: Flowers have white jasmine, dissolving silk, snake navel, hibiscus, cosmos, blue-yellow green sala, jade lotus, cicada purple, water plantain and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Flowers included white jasmine, silk floss, serpent's-navel, hibiscus, cosmos, sala blossoms, jade lotus, purple bauhinia, plantain, and the like.

sentences.zh: 五穀有綠豆、黑豆、麥、稻。

translations.literal: The five grains have green beans, black beans, wheat, rice.
translations.idiomatic: Green and black beans, wheat, and rice were grown.

sentences.zh: 地宜竹。

translations.literal: The ground suits bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo thrived.

sentences.zh: 自昔未嘗朝貢。

translations.literal: From of old it never presented court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Never before had it sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符八年九月，其國主羅茶羅乍遣進奉使侍郎娑里三文、副使蒲恕、判官翁勿、防援官亞勒加等奉表來貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, its state's lord Luochaluo Zha sent presentation envoy vice-minister Suoli Sanwen, vice-envoy Pu Shu, judge Weng Wu, defense officer Yalejia and others bearing a memorial to come and present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of 1015 King Luochaluo Zha of Chola sent the chief envoy Vice Minister Suoli Sanwen, Pu Shu, judge Weng Wu, guard officer Yalejia, and others with a memorial and gifts.

sentences.zh: 三文等以盤奉真珠、碧玻璃升殿，布於御坐前，降殿再拜，譯者導其言曰：「願以表遠人慕化之誠。」

translations.literal: Sanwen and others with trays presented pearls and green glass ascending the hall, spread before the imperial seat, descending the hall bowing again; the interpreter guided their words saying: "I wish with the memorial to express distant people's yearning for transformation."
translations.idiomatic: Sanwen and his party mounted the hall with trays of pearls and green glass laid before the throne, kowtowed again below, and through interpreters said they came to show how far folk yearned toward civilization.

sentences.zh: 其國主表曰：

translations.literal: The state's lord's memorial said:
translations.idiomatic: The king's memorial read:

sentences.zh: 臣羅茶羅乍言，昨遇𦨴舶船商人到本國告稱：钜宋之有天下也，二帝開基，聖人繼統，登封太嶽，禮祀汾陰，至德升聞，上穹眷命。

translations.literal: Subject Luochaluo Zha speaks: recently encountered merchant ships of the state arriving to our country reporting: the great Song's possessing All-under-Heaven, two emperors opening the foundation, sages continuing the succession, ascending to enfeng Mount Tai, performing rites at Fenyin, utmost virtue rising heard, the upper vault entrusting the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Luochaluo Zha reports: merchant ships lately reached us proclaiming that mighty Song holds the realm—two founders laid its base, sages renewed the line, performed the Feng and Shan and the Fenyin sacrifice, virtue heard on high, Heaven's favor confirmed.

sentences.zh: 臣昌期斯遇，吉語幸聞，輒傾就日之誠，仰露朝天之款。

translations.literal: Your subject's prosperous season encountering this, auspicious words fortunately heard, then poured out the sincerity of turning toward the sun, upward revealing the sincere intent of facing the court.
translations.idiomatic: In this propitious hour I heard blessed tidings and bent my heart toward your radiance, declaring before the celestial court.

sentences.zh: 臣伏聞人君之御統也，無遠不臻；

translations.literal: Your subject heard that when a ruler holds the succession, none distant fails to arrive;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a true Son of Heaven leaves no distant shore unvisited;

sentences.zh: 臣子之推誠也，有道則服。

translations.literal: when subjects extend sincerity, where there is the Way they submit.
translations.idiomatic: and subjects who offer sincerity will serve wherever the Way reigns.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下功超邃古，道建大中。

translations.literal: Bow low and think: Your Majesty's achievements surpass remote antiquity, the Way establishes the great Mean.
translations.idiomatic: Your achievements, Sire, outshine antiquity; your Way restores the Grand Mean.

sentences.zh: 衣裳垂而德合乾坤，劍戟鑄而範圍區宇。

translations.literal: Garments hang and virtue joins Heaven and Earth; swords and halberds are cast and the compass embraces the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your robe drapes over Heaven and Earth; your melted blades bound the four seas.

sentences.zh: 神武不殺，人文化成。

translations.literal: Divine martiality does not kill; human culture achieves completion.
translations.idiomatic: By divine martial sway you spare the living; by human civilizing you perfect the realm.

sentences.zh: 廓明明之德以臨御下民，懷翼翼之心以昭事上帝。

translations.literal: Expanding bright virtue to oversee the lower people, harboring cautious hearts to serve the august God.
translations.idiomatic: You brighten virtue to rule the people and keep a wary heart in service to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 至仁不傷於行葦，大信爰及於淵魚。

translations.literal: Utmost benevolence does not harm the walking reed; great trust extends even to the deep fish.
translations.idiomatic: Such benevolence spares even trampled reeds; such faith reaches fish in the deeps.

sentences.zh: 故得天鑒孔彰，帝文有赫，顯今古未聞之事，保家邦大定之基。

translations.literal: Therefore obtaining Heaven's mirror manifestly displayed, the emperor's pattern having splendor, showing events unheard of in present and antiquity, securing the foundation of the state's great settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Heaven's mirror shines clear, imperial glory blazes, wonders unknown in all ages secure your throne and state.

sentences.zh: 竊念臣微類醯雞，賤如芻狗，世居夷落，地遠華風，虛荷燭幽，曾無執贄。

translations.literal: Privately thinking your subject's slight kind is vinegar gnats, vile as straw dogs, generation dwelling in barbarian settlements, land distant from Chinese wind, empty bearing candlelit gloom, never having held tribute gifts.
translations.idiomatic: I, no more than a vinegar fly or straw dog, dwell in barbarian wilds, far from your transforming breeze, lit only by your distant candle, and until now bore no gift.

sentences.zh: 今者竊聽歌頌，普及遐陬。

translations.literal: Now privately hearing songs and praise, universally reaching remote corners.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your praise has reached the farthest corners.

sentences.zh: 恨年屬於桑榆，阻躬陳於玉帛。

translations.literal: I regret years belonging to mulberry and catalpa, blocked from personally presenting jade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Age now ties me like sunset, and I cannot bring jade and silk in person.

sentences.zh: 矧滄溟之曠絕，在跋涉以稍艱。

translations.literal: Moreover the blue sea's vast severance—in trekking and traveling it is somewhat difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The wide ocean too makes the journey arduous.

sentences.zh: 是敢傾倒赤心，遙瞻丹闕。

translations.literal: Therefore I dare pour out the crimson heart, gazing from afar at the cinnabar gate.
translations.idiomatic: So I bare my loyal heart and look from afar toward your vermilion gate.

sentences.zh: 任土作貢，同螻蟻之慕膻；

translations.literal: Rendering earth as tribute, like ants yearning for mutton fat;
translations.idiomatic: I send earth-born tribute as ants crave savory smoke;

sentences.zh: 委質事君，比葵藿之向日。

translations.literal: yielding substance to serve the lord, like sunflowers toward the sun.
translations.idiomatic: I offer my person as sunflowers the sun.

sentences.zh: 謹遣專使等五十二人，奉土物來貢，凡真珠衫帽各一、真珠二萬一千一百兩、象牙六十株、乳香六十斤。

translations.literal: Respectfully sending specially dispatched envoys and others fifty-two persons, presenting local products in tribute—in all pearl shirts and caps each one, pearls twenty-one thousand one hundred taels, ivory sixty stalks, frankincense sixty jin.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject sends fifty-two envoys bearing local tribute: one pearl shirt and cap each, twenty-one thousand one hundred taels of pearls, sixty ivory tusks, and sixty jin of frankincense.

sentences.zh: 三文等又獻珠六千六百兩、香藥三千三百斤。

translations.literal: Sanwen and others also presented pearls six thousand six hundred taels, fragrant drugs three thousand three hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: Sanwen's party added six thousand six hundred taels of pearls and three thousand three hundred jin of aromatics.

sentences.zh: 初，羅茶羅乍既聞商船言，且曰十年來海無風濤，古老傳云如此則中國有聖人，故遣三文等入貢。

translations.literal: Earlier, Luochaluo Zha having heard the merchant ships' words, and said: for ten years the sea has had no wind and waves; old tradition transmits that when it is thus China has a sage, therefore sent Sanwen and others to enter tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Luochaluo Zha heard the merchants, he noted ten years without storms at sea; elders said that meant a sage ruled China—hence Sanwen's embassy.

sentences.zh: 三文離本國，舟行七十七晝夜，曆舟阝勿丹山、娑里西蘭山至占賓國。

translations.literal: Sanwen left his native country; the boat traveled seventy-seven days and nights, passing Zhouwudan Mountain, Suoli Xilan Mountain to Zhanbin Country.
translations.idiomatic: Sanwen sailed seventy-seven days and nights from home, by Zhouwudan and Suoli Xilan to Zhanbin.

sentences.zh: 又行六十一晝夜，曆伊麻羅里山至古羅國。

translations.literal: They sailed another sixty-one days and nights, passing Mount Yimaluoli to reach the state of Gulu.
translations.idiomatic: After another sixty-one days and nights they passed Mount Yimaluoli and reached Gulu.

sentences.zh: 國有古羅山，因名焉。

translations.literal: The state has Mount Gulu, from which it takes its name.
translations.idiomatic: The country took its name from Mount Gulu.

sentences.zh: 又行七十一晝夜，曆加八山、占不牢山、舟寶龍山至三佛齊國。

translations.literal: They sailed another seventy-one days and nights, passing Mount Jiaba, Mount Zhanbulao, and Mount Zhoubaolong to reach the state of Srivijaya.
translations.idiomatic: After seventy-one more days and nights they passed Mount Jiaba, Mount Zhanbulao, and Mount Zhoubaolong and arrived at Srivijaya.

sentences.zh: 又行十八晝夜，度蠻山水口，曆天竺山，至賓頭狼山，望東西王母塚，距舟所將百里。

translations.literal: They sailed another eighteen days and nights, crossed the Man Mountain estuary, passed Mount Tianzhu, reached Mount Bintoulang, and gazed upon the eastern and western tombs of the Queen Mother of the West, about a hundred li from where the ship lay.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen days and nights later they crossed the Man Mountain estuary, passed Mount Tianzhu, and reached Mount Bintoulang, whence the eastern and western tombs of the Queen Mother of the West could be seen about a hundred li from the anchorage.

sentences.zh: 又行二十晝夜，度羊山、九星山至廣州之琵琶洲。

translations.literal: They sailed another twenty days and nights, passed Mount Yang and Mount Jiuxing, and reached Pipa Islet at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty days and nights later they passed Mount Yang and Mount Jiuxing and reached Pipa Islet at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 離本國凡千一百五十日至廣州焉。

translations.literal: From their homeland to Guangzhou was in all one thousand one hundred fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: The voyage from their homeland to Guangzhou took altogether 1,150 days.

sentences.zh: 詔閣門祗候史祐之館伴，凡宴賜恩例同龜茲使。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Gate Attendant Shi Youzhi to serve as host; all banquets, gifts, and gracious precedents were the same as for Kucha envoys.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Gate Attendant Shi Youzhi as host; banquets and gifts followed the same precedent as for Kucha missions.

sentences.zh: 其年承天節，三文等請於啟聖禪院會僧以祝聖壽。

translations.literal: That year on the Chengtian festival, Sanwen and others asked to gather monks at Qisheng Chan Monastery to pray for the sage emperor's longevity.
translations.idiomatic: That year at the Chengtian festival Sanwen and others asked to assemble monks at Qisheng Chan Monastery to pray for the emperor's long life.

sentences.zh: 明年使回，降詔羅茶羅乍，賜物甚厚。

translations.literal: The next year when the envoys returned, an edict was sent down to Luochaluo Zha and gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys returned the following year, an edict went to King Luochaluo Zha with very generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，又遣使琶攔得麻烈呧奉物入貢，至廣州病死。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi, they again sent the envoy Palande Maliechu to present tribute goods; he reached Guangzhou and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1020 they sent Palande Maliechu with tribute again; he reached Guangzhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 守臣以其表聞。

translations.literal: The defending official reported his memorial to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The local commander forwarded his memorial to court.

sentences.zh: 詔廣州宴犒從者，厚賜以遣之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Guangzhou to feast and reward the followers and send them off with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Guangzhou to feast the retinue, reward them generously, and send them home.

sentences.zh: 明道二年十月，其王屍離囉茶印�囉注囉遣使蒲押陀離等以泥金表進真珠衫帽及真珠一百五兩、象牙百株，西染院副使、閣門通事舍人符惟忠假鴻臚少卿押伴。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Mingdao, its king Shili Luocha Yinluo Zhuluo sent envoys Pu Yatuoli and others with a gold-dust memorial presenting a pearl shirt and cap, one hundred five taels of pearls, and one hundred elephant tusks; Fu Weizhong, vice-director of the Western Dyeing Institute and Gate Communicator Attendant, was temporarily made Vice Director of the Court for Ceremonials to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of 1033 King Shili Luocha Yinluo Zhuluo sent Pu Yatuoli and others with a gold-dust memorial, a pearl shirt and cap, 105 taels of pearls, and 100 ivory tusks; Fu Weizhong of the Western Dyeing Institute and the Gate Office served as acting Vice Director of the Court for Ceremonials as escort.

sentences.zh: 蒲押陀離自言數朝貢，而海風破船不達，願將上等珠就龍床腳撒殿，頂戴瞻禮，以申向慕之心。

translations.literal: Pu Yatuoli said himself that he had presented tribute many times but sea winds wrecked the ships and he could not arrive; he wished to bring fine pearls to scatter before the hall at the foot of the dragon couch, to wear them on his head and gaze in worship, thereby expressing his heart of admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Yatuoli said he had come to court many times but storms had wrecked his ships; he now wished to scatter fine pearls before the throne at the foot of the dragon couch, place them on his head, and bow in worship to express his devotion.

sentences.zh: 乃奉銀盤升殿，跪撒珠於御榻下而退。

translations.literal: He then bore a silver tray up to the hall, knelt, scattered pearls beneath the imperial couch, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He then ascended with a silver tray, knelt, scattered pearls beneath the imperial couch, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 景祐元年二月，以蒲押陀離爲金紫光祿大夫、懷化將軍，還本國。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jingyou, Pu Yatuoli was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Purple Pouch and Huaihua General, and returned to his country.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1034 Pu Yatuoli was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Purple Pouch and Huaihua General and sent home.

sentences.zh: 熙寧十年，國王地華加羅遣使奇囉囉、副使南卑琶打、判官麻圖華羅等二十七人來獻踠豆珠、麻珠、琉璃大洗盤、白梅花腦、錦藥、犀牙、乳香、瓶香、薔薇水、金蓮花、木香、阿魏、鵬砂、丁香。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xining, King Dihuajialuo sent envoys Qiluoluo, vice-envoy Nanbeipada, judge Matuhualuo, and twenty-seven others to present wando beads, hemp beads, a large glass washing basin, white plum-blossom borneol, brocade medicines, rhinoceros horn, frankincense, bottled incense, rose water, golden lotus, aloeswood, asafoetida, pengsha, and cloves.
translations.idiomatic: In 1077 King Dihuajialuo sent Qiluoluo, Nanbeipada, Matuhualuo, and twenty-seven others with wando and hemp beads, a large glass basin, white plum-blossom borneol, brocade medicines, rhinoceros horn, frankincense, bottled incense, rose water, golden lotus, aloeswood, asafoetida, pengsha, and cloves.

sentences.zh: 使副以真珠、龍腦登陛，跪而散之，謂之撒殿。

translations.literal: The envoy and vice-envoy ascended the steps with pearls and borneol, knelt and scattered them—this was called "scattering before the hall."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy and vice-envoy ascended with pearls and borneol, knelt, and scattered them in the rite called "scattering before the hall."

sentences.zh: 既降，詔遣御藥宣勞之，以爲懷化將軍、保順郎將，各賜衣服器幣有差；

translations.literal: After they descended, an edict sent imperial medicines to proclaim consolation; they were made Huaihua Generals and Baoshun Lang generals, each granted clothing and vessels in graded amounts;
translations.idiomatic: After they withdrew, the court sent imperial medicines as consolation, appointed them Huaihua Generals and Baoshun Lang generals, and granted graded robes and gifts;

sentences.zh: 答賜其王錢八萬一千八百緡、銀五萬二千兩。

translations.literal: In reply their king was granted eighty-one thousand eight hundred strings of cash and fifty-two thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Their king received in return 81,800 strings of cash and 52,000 taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 丹眉流

translations.literal: Tambralinga.
translations.idiomatic: Tambralinga.

sentences.zh: 丹眉流國，東至占臘五十程，南至羅越水路十五程，西至西天三十五程，北至程良六十程，東北至羅斛二十五程，東南至闍婆四十五程，西南至程若十五程，西北至洛華二十五程，東北至廣州一百三十五程。

translations.literal: The state of Tambralinga: east to Zhanla fifty stages, south to Luoyue by water fifteen stages, west to the Western Heaven thirty-five stages, north to Chengliang sixty stages, northeast to Luoqu twenty-five stages, southeast to Java forty-five stages, southwest to Chengruo fifteen stages, northwest to Luohua twenty-five stages, northeast to Guangzhou one hundred thirty-five stages.
translations.idiomatic: Tambralinga lay fifty stages east of Zhanla, fifteen stages south by water to Luoyue, thirty-five stages west to India, sixty stages north to Chengliang, twenty-five stages northeast to Luoqu, forty-five stages southeast to Java, fifteen stages southwest to Chengruo, twenty-five stages northwest to Luohua, and 135 stages northeast to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其俗以版爲屋；

translations.literal: Their custom is to make houses of planks;
translations.idiomatic: They built houses of planks;

sentences.zh: 跣足，衣布，無紳帶，以白紵纏其首；

translations.literal: they go barefoot, wear cloth, have no sashes, and wrap white ramie about the head;
translations.idiomatic: went barefoot, wore cloth without sashes, and wrapped white ramie about the head;

sentences.zh: 貿易以金銀。

translations.literal: trade is conducted in gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: and traded in gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 其主所居，廣袤五里，無城郭；

translations.literal: Where the ruler dwells is five li in breadth and length, without walled cities;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's residence covered five li square without walled cities;

sentences.zh: 出則乘象車，亦有小駟。

translations.literal: when he goes out he rides an elephant carriage, and there are also small teams of horses.
translations.idiomatic: when he went abroad he rode an elephant carriage or a small horse team.

sentences.zh: 地出犀、象、鍮石、紫草、蘇木諸藥。

translations.literal: The land produces rhinoceros horn, elephants, brass, purple root, sappanwood, and various medicines.
translations.idiomatic: The land yielded rhinoceros horn, elephants, brass, purple root, sappanwood, and other drugs.

sentences.zh: 四時炎熱，無雪霜。

translations.literal: All four seasons are hot; there is no snow or frost.
translations.idiomatic: All seasons were hot; snow and frost were unknown.

sentences.zh: 未嘗至中國。

translations.literal: They had never come to China.
translations.idiomatic: Before this they had never reached China.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，國主多須機遣使打吉馬、副使打臘、判官皮泥等九人來貢木香千斤、鍮镴各百斤、胡黃連三十五斤、紫草百斤、紅氈一合、花布四段、蘇木萬斤、象牙六十一株。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping, King Duoxuji sent envoys Dajima, vice-envoy Dala, judge Pini, and nine others to present one thousand jin of aloeswood, one hundred jin each of brass and pewter, thirty-five jin of Tibetan coptis, one hundred jin of purple root, one set of red felt, four bolts of patterned cloth, ten thousand jin of sappanwood, and sixty-one elephant tusks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1001 King Duoxuji sent Dajima, Dala, Pini, and nine others with 1,000 jin of aloeswood, 100 jin each of brass and pewter, 35 jin of Tibetan coptis, 100 jin of purple root, red felt, four bolts of patterned cloth, 10,000 jin of sappanwood, and 61 ivory tusks.

sentences.zh: 召見崇德殿，賜以冠帶服物。

translations.literal: They were summoned to audience at Chongde Hall and granted caps, belts, and garments.
translations.idiomatic: They were received at Chongde Hall and granted caps, belts, and robes.

sentences.zh: 及還，又賜多須機詔書以敦獎之。

translations.literal: When they returned, Duoxuji was also granted an edict to encourage and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: On their return an edict was sent to Duoxuji to commend and encourage him.
